Were any current Man City players signed during charges period?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester City captain Ruben Dias has made more than 250 club appearances since his arrival in 2020.
  • No member of Manchester City's current squad was signed during the period in which an independent commission found the club guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations.
  • Those offences all came between 2009 and 2018.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City captain Ruben Dias has made more than 250 club appearances since his arrival in 2020.

No member of Manchester City's current squad was signed during the period in which an independent commission found the club guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations.

Those offences all came between 2009 and 2018. City have denied any wrongdoing and appealed against all of the charges against them.

The club's longest-serving first-team player who was purchased from another club is Portuguese centre-back and club captain Ruben Dias, who joined from Benfica in 2020.

Norway striker Erling Haaland is the next longest-serving arrival, joining from Borussia Dortmund in the summer of 2022.

Midfielder Phil Foden is the only player to have played for the club during the period in which they breached the league's financial rules, but was not a senior signing having come through the club's youth ranks.

Foden, 26, made his first-team debut in a Champions League match against Feyenoord in November 2017.

Like Foden, versatile midfielder Rico Lewis is also a product of the club's academy but did not make his senior debut until August 2022.

All of the club's other senior players were signed between 2023 and 2026.

Industry News: Who is close to a yellow card suspension in Champions League?

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (358 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal forward Kai Havertz is among the players to have received two yellow cards in this season's Champions League.
  • Players will receive a one-match ban should they receive four yellow cards before the semi-finals of the Champions League.
  • This rule runs from the start of the league phase until the end of the quarter-finals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal forward Kai Havertz is among the players to have received two yellow cards in this season's Champions League.

Players will receive a one-match ban should they receive four yellow cards before the semi-finals of the Champions League.

This rule runs from the start of the league phase until the end of the quarter-finals. After then, all yellow cards are wiped out and players cannot be suspended for multiple yellow cards.

Yellow cards that result in a red card during a match do not count towards a player's tally, as a separate suspension will be served.

The same rules apply for both the Europa League and the Conference League.

During the opening three rounds of the Champions League, 16 players received two yellow cards, meaning they are now two cautions away from a one-match ban.

Shakhtar Donetsk's Marlon Gomes, Villarreal's Santiago Mourino and Inter Milan's Hakan Calhanoglu are each on three yellow cards, putting them on the brink of a ban.

Players can also be suspended if they pick up six, eight or 10 yellow cards. This would also result in a one-match suspension every time a player hits an even number of yellow cards above four.

Red cards result in a one-match suspension, with Bayern Munich's Michael Olise missing his side's earlier clash with Arsenal after being sent off against Viking in the previous round of fixtures.

Uefa may increase the length of a red card ban for serious offences such as violent conduct.

Marlon Gomes (Shakhtar Donetsk).

Josko Gvardiol (Manchester City).

Matheus Cunha* (Manchester United).

Alessandro Bastoni* (Inter Milan).

Cristian Martinez (Slovan Bratislava).

Alexis Mac Allister (Liverpool).

*denotes two yellows that resulted in a red card.

The following players will miss the next round of league phase matches following either a yellow or red card suspension:.

Matheus Cunha (Manchester United - red card suspension).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, we probably don't need to recap the story, do we? But just in case...

It was 30 years ago exactly, back on 23 November, 1996, when Ali Dia made perhaps the most notorious appearance in the history of Premier League football.

Dia had purported to be the cousin of George Weah to get himself a trial at Graeme Souness' Southampton, and incredibly ended up coming on in place of the injured Matt Le Tissier, only to later be subbed back off hauled back off in the 85th minute of a 2-0 defeat to Leeds.

Dia looked like he'd struggle to play in a Sunday league team, never mind a top-flight outfit - but as Souness explained to FourFourTwo: "That was portrayed like we'd been conned, but no-one was conned.

"Someone phoned up pretending to be George Weah, but we were getting players in every month to come on trial, because we had no money – that's where we got Eyal Berkovic." (Wonder who Berkovic's agent pretended to be?).

"When we got the call about Dia, I said, 'Get him in'.

"Within the first five minutes of a small-sided game at training, I realised he wasn't good enough for us.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

"But we didn't have enough players for training sessions, so we mentioned, 'We'll keep him until the end of the week, then we'll tell him'.

"That week we got more and more injuries, to the point where my coach Terry Cooper mentioned, 'We're going to have to have that clown on the bench'.

In a recent development, "I mentioned, 'We can't'. He said, 'We haven't got any players'.

"He was on the bench against Leeds, then Matt Le Tissier comes off injured and I've got a choice between a centre-half, a full-back or a defensive midfielder [or Dia].

"I noted, 'Stick Dia on, he'll run about, hopefully occupy their back four'.

"He did that, but he was out of his depth.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Steven Pressley revealed the embarrassment of Dundee’s 8-0 hammering by Hearts on Saturday left him wanting to “crawl under a rock and hide”.

The Dark Blues manager has shouldered full responsibility after his team suffered their heaviest-ever home league defeat.

Industry observers note that speaking as Dundee prepared to return to action at Hibernian on Tuesday, Pressley said: “It’s been a difficult 24-48 hours. There’s been a lot of hurt, a lot of embarrassment. As you can imagine, at times I’ve wanted to crawl under a rock and hide.

In a recent development, “It’s difficult on the back of such a disappointing result. But I will say this, I suffer a lot from vulnerability at times, but for some reason during difficult moments I seem to find strength from somewhere.

“I don’t know if it’s from my family, from messages that I’ve received, from my reading.

Industry observers note that “But I’ve had to show strength, I have to support the players. I have to make sure we navigate our way out of what was a really embarrassing moment.

Sources indicate that “We had a good meeting yesterday. We chatted a lot about the various aspects, and hopefully we can start responding to the disappointment.”.

Pressley remarked he had feared a setback coming for Dundee – “not 8-0 but a disappointing performance” – because he had “sensed a little bit of subconscious complacency”.

The manager felt his team had been over-hyped by outsiders on the back of a start to the season in which they won five of their 12 matches before the international break.

“We’re nowhere near the levels that people keep telling us we are,” he stressed. “We’re not a good enough team not to do the hard yards. Our whole strength has been built on the cohesion of the team, the unity of the team, the aggressiveness of the team.

Sources indicate that “And I think what Saturday did highlight is exactly what I’ve been saying. If we get lazy on the hard yards, we’re a very vulnerable team.

“We have to be at our absolute best to get results. If we fall below that, we’re nowhere near the levels that people have been telling us we’re at.”.

Sources indicate that pressley said Saturday has to represent “a reset moment, a moment we can always come back to to help us become better”. Asked if he expected a positive response from his players at Easter Road just 72 hours on from their Hearts humbling, he said: “I don’t know.

In a recent development, “I know that they’re hurting. I know that they want to respond in the best possible way. That part I don’t question. I know how much it’s affected them.

Industry observers note that “But we’ve not had a lot of time. I just hope we can bring some pride back to the football club with the right type of performance.”.

Latest Update: Which game will Chelsea's Palmer miss after red card?

📅 26 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (280 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cole Palmer was sent off in the second half of Chelsea's 2-0 loss at Stamford Bridge.
  • Chelsea's Cole Palmer will not miss the Blues' Premier League meeting with Manchester United on Saturday, despite being sent off in his side's last Premier League match.
  • Industry observers note that palmer was shown two yellow cards in the second half of the Blues' defeat by rivals Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cole Palmer was sent off in the second half of Chelsea's 2-0 loss at Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea's Cole Palmer will not miss the Blues' Premier League meeting with Manchester United on Saturday, despite being sent off in his side's last Premier League match.

Industry observers note that palmer was shown two yellow cards in the second half of the Blues' defeat by rivals Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday. That dismissal meant that Palmer was handed a one-match ban.

According to recent reports, the England playmaker was shown his first caution for an off-the-ball incident involving Spurs' Mateus Fernandes. He was then shown a second yellow card for a foul on Conor Gallagher.

In most cases, this would be served in that team's next Premier League match. However, Palmer will not miss Chelsea's meeting with United at Stamford Bridge.

Instead, Palmer will be banned for the Blues' EFL Cup fourth-round match away at Liverpool on Wednesday night.

This is because red card suspensions are carried out across domestic competitions rather than being specific to the competition they were received in.

Suspensions for an accumulation of yellow cards across a campaign are served in the competition in which they are received.

So while the Blues will miss Palmer for their trip to Anfield, he will be available to face United three days after the club's cup tie on Merseyside.

The Premier League is a one-horse race but the real drama in European football is happening in Italy

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (650 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fourfourtwo

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you're looking for jeopardy at the top of the Premier League this season, you're looking in the wrong place.
  • Arsenal, already reigning champions, have so far turned their title defence into an autumn stroll, swatting aside challengers with efficiency, threatening to wrap up another crown at a canter before winter is even through.
  • For genuine drama and unpredictability in 2026/27, the centre of gravity in European football has shifted south.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you're looking for jeopardy at the top of the Premier League this season, you're looking in the wrong place.

Arsenal, already reigning champions, have so far turned their title defence into an autumn stroll, swatting aside challengers with efficiency, threatening to wrap up another crown at a canter before winter is even through.

For genuine drama and unpredictability in 2026/27, the centre of gravity in European football has shifted south. Serie A, once a league renowned for miserly defences and low-scoring contests, is serving up the most compelling, wide-open title race on the continent.

If any proof was needed that Italian football has buried its old catenaccio stereotype for good, Sunday evening's 4-4 draw between Atalanta and Inter Milan delivered it.

Far from being a cagey affair, it was pure mayhem with two heavyweights trading blows right up until the final whistle.

That eight-goal epic was no anomaly, either because across Europe’s top five leagues this campaign, Serie A actually leads the way for entertainment in front of goal, averaging 3.08 goals per match.

Industry observers note that the Italian top flight is comfortably ahead of the Bundesliga (2.94), the Premier League (2.81), Ligue 1 (2.72) and La Liga (2.56). So, forget 1-0 defensive masterclasses, modern calcio is all about goals.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

In a recent development, better still, the table looks like a throwback to the division’s 1990s golden era. Only a handful of points separates the leading pack, with several of Italy’s biggest and best-supported institutions - from Milan and Naples to Turin and the capital - are engaged in a multi-club scrap for the Scudetto.

A key reason for that is the capital roaring back to life. Both Roma and Lazio remain unbeaten 12 games into the season, having spent too many recent campaigns watching their northern rivals monopolise domestic success. The Eternal City’s old powers are title contenders once again, playing with renewed swagger.

The beauty of this Serie A season lies just as much in its new blood as its established giants, becaause perched on the periphery of the title race are Como, one of European football’s coolest and most compelling stories.

Recent findings suggest that their lakeside glamour is neatly juxtaposed by a smart, progressive sporting project and exciting football. They are doing their best to crash the elite party without a hint of an inferiority complex.

For nearly a decade, Juventus’ run of nine consecutive titles drained the suspense from Italian football. Serie A has since become one of Europe’s most competitive major leagues, albeit without continental success. Over the past five years, three different clubs - Inter, AC Milan and Napoli - have lifted the trophy, and not once has it returned to Turin, nor does it look as though that'll be the case this season, either.

Of course, the Premier League still boasts the deepest pockets and the best marketing machine, but when the title race is effectively over before December, spectacle suffers. In Italy, the potential for plot twists retains the intrigue and drama.

Sources indicate that arsenal were cruising. This was life on Premier League easy street, but from complete control of this game against Newcastle United, they tossed it away. It was a spectacular, unexpected implosion. They were extremely fortunate to escape with a point.

You cannot switch off away from home in the Premier League and you certainly can never be complacent against a team with Newcastle’s home crowd behind them.

It has been revealed that from control to disarray. From looking like champions, Arsenal, who also lost goalkeeper David Raya to a worrying looking injury, rumbled under pressure. To go from dominance to being grateful for a draw, this was a flaky side of the Premier League leaders we have not seen for a while.

Industry observers note that “We have lost two points,” said manager Mikel Arteta. “We were exceptional in the first half, the intensity and the quality, we should have been two, three or four goals up.

Recent findings suggest that “When you don’t do that, in the second half you cannot give the opposition belief and you cannot give them goals. We did both. We started to lose duels, second balls, we gave it away.”.

Was it arrogance? Did the title-holders start to believe they were simply too good to be hurt or worried by a team with Newcastle’s obvious limitations? It looked like it. The way Arsenal fell apart as soon as the momentum in the game shifted in the home team’s favour in the second half was shocking.

In a recent development, newcastle were dreadful before the break and managed just one attack before half-time. Perhaps it was all too easy for Arteta’s side. They have become used to ferocious battles on Tyneside, but this was a stroll for 45 minutes. When it turned into a proper test after half-time, though, they folded.

To give the opposition one goal against the run of play can be forgiven, but to do it a second time, when the heat is cranked up, hints at a fragility we no longer thought existed under Arteta.

Sources indicate that the first goal came from a blunder by captain Martin Odegaard. It was a lazy, sloppy swing of the leg to try to clear a throw-in and the ball sliced backwards. When it looped into the path of Will Osula, he squared to the unmarked Harvey Barnes who put away the equaliser comfortably.

According to recent reports, if this is the vertical football Matthias Jaissle has preached since he arrived in August, Newcastle supporters can buy into it. There was speed, a physicality and a boldness in this second-half performance. It was fun and exciting. It was football played on the front foot. It was what we were promised when the German replaced Eddie Howe.

It has been revealed that “That is Newcastle’s DNA, the second half is what we want this team to play like,” remarked Jaissle. “We knew there would be ups and downs this season, but if we can put that performance together for 90 minutes we can definitely say we are moving in the right direction.”.

Industry observers note that the problem is, Newcastle have not put a 90-minute performance like this together all season. We have only seen it in flashes and as good as the second half was, we cannot lose sight of the fact the first was abject. Newcastle’s football was aimless, clueless and dysfunctional. One attack before the break, one deflected shot wide is simply not good enough.

The transformation at half-time was unexpected. The substitutes helped; Tino Livramento was a massive upgrade on Amar Dedic at right-back, Jacob Ramsey improved the midfield and Anthony Elanga brought speed and, yes, a vertical threat to their attack.

But Jaissle’s side did not hold on for the win. They had the chances to score a third, but it was their ambition to do so that caused their downfall. Arsenal’s class shone again, passing through the lines to release Noni Madueke.

And it should have been 2-0, 3-0 or 4-0 up, clear.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yeremy Pino is the latest Premier League player to receive a yellow-card suspension.

Crystal Palace's Yeremy Pino has become the latest Premier League player to receive a yellow card suspension after accumulating five bookings since the 2026-27 season began.

Hull City's Matt Crooks and Aston Villa's Matty Cash were the first players to receive a ban for collecting five yellow cards before gameweek 19.

Players receive a one-match suspension if they pick up five or more yellow cards prior to the conclusion of their team's 19th league match of the season.

There are now 18 players sitting on four bookings after 11 rounds of matches, meaning they must avoid another yellow card prior to the halfway point of the season to avoid a ban.

Bournemouth have the most players on the brink of a ban, with three players one yellow card away from suspension.

After that date, the threshold increases to 10 yellow cards. Any player reaching that number before the end of their club's 32nd league match of the season will receive a two-match suspension.

From that point, there are further thresholds at 15 and 20 yellow cards.

It has been revealed that for players reaching 15 cautions, they incur a three-match suspension. Punishments for players reaching 20 yellow cards are determined by a regulatory commission.

Those cut-offs do not reset until the end of the Premier League season.

In the Championship, League One and League Two, there are similar thresholds.

However, with those three divisions having 46 rounds of league matches instead of 38, players have to avoid getting 10 yellow cards before the end of the 37th league match in order to not receive a two-match suspension.

In those divisions, the yellow cards are reset at the end of the league season and do not include matches in the play-offs.

The following players have received a one-match ban and will now receive a two-match ban if they reach ten bookings before game week 32:.

Yeremy Pino - Crystal Palace (five yellow cards).

Matt Crooks - Hull City (five yellow cards).

Matty Cash - Aston Villa (five).

If any of the following players receive another Premier League yellow card before the season's halfway point, they will be banned for one match:.

Vitaly Janelt - Brentford (four).

Oli McBurnie - Hull City (four).

Harry Maguire - Manchester United (four).

Pascal Gross - Brighton & Hove Albion (four).

Ethan Ampadu - Leeds United (four).

Antonio Silva - Bournemouth (four).

Alexis Mac Allister - Liverpool (four).

James McAtee - Nottingham Forest (four).

Chema Andres - Brighton & Hove Albion (four).

Bradley Barcola - Liverpool (four).

Murillo - Nottingham Forest (four).

The following players will miss their club's next set of fixtures:.

Yeremy Pino - Crytsal Palce (yellow card suspension).

Jean-Philippe Mateta - Crystal Palace (red card suspension).

Igor Thiago - Brentford (red card suspension).

Costinha - Brighton & Hove Albion (red card suspension).

Hashim Thaci's second conviction in The Hague reignites debate in Kosovo about justice and the Kosovo Specialist Chambers

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (891 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A court in The Hague on Tuesday convicted former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci of obstructing justice and attempting to influence witnesses during his recent war crimes trial and sentenced him to 17 months in prison.
  • This term will be added to his 25-year sentence for war crimes, which was handed down by the same court, the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, on September 16.
  • According to the indictment of the Specialist Prosecutor's Office, Thaci had provided visitors at the detention facility in The Hague with confidential information about witnesses in his war crimes trial and had instructed them on how to influence their testimony.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A court in The Hague on Tuesday convicted former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci of obstructing justice and attempting to influence witnesses during his recent war crimes trial and sentenced him to 17 months in prison.

This term will be added to his 25-year sentence for war crimes, which was handed down by the same court, the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, on September 16.

According to the indictment of the Specialist Prosecutor's Office, Thaci had provided visitors at the detention facility in The Hague with confidential information about witnesses in his war crimes trial and had instructed them on how to influence their testimony.

Three other men — former head of the Kosovo Intelligence Agency Bashkim Smakaj, former Minister of Justice Hajredin Kuci, and Fadil Fazliu — were also convicted.

Thaci, who was the former political leader of the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) during the 1998-1999 Kosovo War, is viewed by many in his home country as a hero. His war crimes conviction in September was greeted in Kosovo with anger and dismay.

Thaci has vowed to appeal the war crimes conviction.

Sources indicate that his two convictions touch deep sensitivities in Kosovo society. Tuesday's ruling brings renewed attention to the war that ended 27 years ago, the role played by its former leaders, and the continuing debate over justice, individual or collective responsibility for the KLA's war to liberate Kosovo from Serbia, and trust in judicial institutions.

The response from the government of Kosovo was swift.

In a recent development, in a statement issued on Tuesday, the government noted, "Trust in justice is built not only on the decisions that are made, but also on the manner in which they are reached. Therefore, our commitment to the rule of law and our insistence on the full respect of rights and procedural guarantees are part of the same principled position: Justice must not only be done, but must also be fair, transparent, and credible.".

The Kosovo Specialist Chambers was established in 2015 by the parliament of Kosovo at the instigation of the European Union and the United States.

The court was created to investigate serious crimes allegedly committed by members of the KLA during and after the Kosovo War.

For security reasons, including concerns about witness intimidation, the court was located in The Hague in the Netherlands.

After Thaci and three others were convicted of war crimes in first instance in September, Kosovo's state authorities established a working group to draft a strategy regarding the appeal proceedings before the Kosovo Specialist Chambers.

The group is chaired by Foreign Minister Glauk Konjufca and includes members of Kosovo's parliament.

Prime Minister Albin Kurti has stated that the working group continues to believe that "the first-instance judgment of the Specialist Chambers is unjust, both legally and morally," and that as a result, "the government is working to secure a correction at the appeals level before the Specialist Chambers.".

In addition, the parliament of Kosovo is currently considering amendments to the law governing the Kosovo Specialist Chambers.

The draft law, which is expected to be adopted, envisages narrowing the court's mandate in several areas, including the time period covered by its jurisdiction, limiting the maximum prison sentence to 15 years, allowing sentences to be served in Kosovo, and introducing the possibility of presidential pardons for persons convicted by final court decisions.

How do political analysts and legal experts view the parliament's attempt to amend the law on the Kosovo Specialist Chambers before the judicial process involving the four men convicted of war crimes has reached a final verdict?

"From an international perspective, at first glance, this initiative could even be interpreted as an attempt to interfere in the judicial process," noted political analyst and university professor Artan Muhaxheri.

"Precisely for this reason, it is essential that Kosovo's political spectrum and its legal experts demonstrate beyond any doubt that this measure does not conflict with Kosovo's international obligations toward the European Union," Muhaxheri told DW, adding that this is the only way to ensure that the desired outcome is achieved and that the initiative does not produce the opposite effect.

"Concerns relating to jurisdiction, statutory limits on maximum sentences, and other similar matters must be argued professionally and rigorously, demonstrating that they fully guarantee judicial independence and enjoy solid support within Kosovo's legal system, the same legal system that, first and foremost, established the Specialist Chambers," he said.

Ehat Miftaraj, executive director of the Kosovo Law Institute (IKD), told DW that although the Kosovo Specialist Chambers were established by the Republic of Kosovo itself, "the way the judicial process has unfolded has created the impression that judges, prosecutors and certain international actors have treated not only the accused but also Kosovo itself with distrust, prejudice, and an often condescending approach.".

Miftaraj went on to say that reactions and objections in Kosovo to the decisions of the Specialist Chambers are also interpreted and judged in the historical and emotional context of the war and what Kosovo's citizens experienced during and after it.

"In a democratic society, every citizen, including political and institutional representatives, has the right to criticize judicial decisions," he said. "However, there is a fundamental distinction between criticism based on legal arguments and attempts to delegitimize courts or exert influence over judicial proceedings. And here, there is room for criticism of both sides.".

England are a seeded side for the Nations League quarter-finals after topping their group.

The draw for the final eight teams in the 2026-27 Nations League will be on Friday, 20 November at 11:00 GMT.

It will take place at Uefa's headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland and be broadcast on Uefa TV.

England are the only home nation to have made it to the quarter-final stage, however Northern Ireland's draw against Hungary saw them top Group B2 and secure promotion to League A in the 2028-29 tournament.

Scotland will remain in League B following their third-place finish in Group B1, and Wales face a League A/B relegation play-off in March after being consigned to last place in Group A4.

The Republic of Ireland finished second in Group B3 and so will take part in a League A/B promotion play-off in March.

The winners of groups A1-A4 are seeded for the draw, playing the runners-up of other groups in League A.

England have sealed their place in the last eight as Group A3 winners and could face:.

They cannot face A3 runners-up Spain as teams must be drawn against sides from other groups.

The quarter-finals will be played over two legs during the international break between 25-30 March.

Seeded teams get to play the second leg of their quarter-final at home.

Nations that reach the semi-finals can bid those penultimate matches as well as the final.

The remaining dates for the Nations League are:.

Quarter-finals first leg: 25-27 March.

Quarter-finals second leg: 28-30 March.

Semi-finals, third-place play-off and final: 9-13 June.

The home nations expect Fifa to be in a “different place” by the time they host the Women’s World Cup in 2035 after withdrawing their support for president Gianni Infantino earlier this year.

The joint bid from England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales was approved at the Fifa Congress on Monday, although it was the sole bidder to host the 48-team tournament and was voted through by acclamation.

The tournament will be the first World Cup to be held in the UK since England hosted the men’s World Cup in 1966, but it comes just months after the chair of the English FA, Debbie Hewitt, demanded an independent investigation into Infantino’s scrapped World Cup sell-off initiative and the Folarin Balogun affair, as well calls for further Fifa reform.

Infantino has retained the support required for re-election in March but cannot continue beyond 2031, and the FA’s director of women’s football Sue Day believes there will be significant change within Fifa as the home nations prepare to work alongside the governing body on staging the World Cup in 2035.

There have already been some challenges, with Fifa reportedly demanding tax-free status from ticket sales and broadcast and commercial partnerships, something that the UK government has not allowed when previously hosting major events such as the 2012 Olympics and will not offer to Uefa when they stage Euro 2028.

“There are two separate problems here, the concerns around the Fifa leadership and their proposals, and then this World Cup,” Day stated on Monday.

“We very much want today to be about the excitement of this World Cup and we didn't want those concerns to get in the way of us trying to land the opportunity to put on this amazing tournament that we think can change the world of football.

Industry observers note that “By the time the tournament comes around, lots of things will have changed. We expect Fifa to be in a different place.

“We know that there is a brilliant team there right now, led by Jill Ellis [former USA manager, now Fifa’s Chief Football Officer], leading women’s football and we're really looking forward to working with them on developing the tournament.”.

Day also said that the home nations hope to have a “strong influence” on the pricing of the tournament. Fifa were accused of “betrayal” and price gouging when the ticket prices were revealed for last summer’s men’s World Cup in North American last summer but tickets for the 2027 Women’s World Cup in Brazil will go on sale for as little as £4 next month.

But Fifa is targeting revenues of $4bn when it stages the first 48-team World Cup in 2031, in the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica, and will be setting similar targets for the England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales bid.

It has been revealed that “At the moment, the model is absolutely that Fifa decides those things,” Day said. “We will hope to be able to have a really strong influence on some of that because we know our audiences best.

Sources indicate that “It’s going to be really important to get the pricing right. We all know that we need to show the commercial viability of women’s football, and we want this to be an accessible tournament.”.

A 48-team Women’s World Cup would see the UK will host 104 matches across 39 days in 2035, in the largest single-sport event ever to be staged in the country, and Day said success for the tournament will be judged on its potential to transform society as well as what happens on the pitch.

According to recent reports, “This is genuinely once in a lifetime, once in a generation,” Day noted. “There wouldn’t have been a World Cup on this soil since 1966, which would be nearly 70 years away.

“And so I think just collectively, I want us to grasp the opportunity of this moment and really build towards it and think of it as, it will be the most amazing tournament, but it's [also] a catalyst for growth and inspiration and something to springboard from.

Sources indicate that “I think we can change the world a little bit with the tournament and we should aim that high. Why wouldn't we aim that high?”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aston Villa were expecting some teething problems in 2026/27, but not being able to rely on home wins keeping them on track probably wasn’t one of them.

Industry observers note that villa seldom looked capable of breaking the deadlock in Saturday’s goalless draw with Sunderland. Their 2-1 win over Manchester City was their only home win in the Premier League in six attempts this season.

It’s a far cry from the general shape of Villa’s home from since Unai Emery took over as manager in the autumn of 2022. Villa Park has been the bedrock of the Emery revolution, but it’s anything but impenetrable so far this term.

Last season ended in triumph both in the fight for Champions League places and in the Europa League, but Villa’s faltering home form dates back to the start of 2026.

They won their first home match after the turn of the year but they lost their first home match for nearly four months when Everton visited Birmingham and won 1-0 in the middle of January. It was the same result against Brentford in the next home fixture and the aura, suddenly, was weakened.

A spate of midfield injuries affected those matches but Villa’s home form since Upcoming Year’s Day includes as many losses as wins in the league – six of each – and failures this season to beat Nottingham Forest (now 17th in the table), Fulham (15th) and Sunderland (19th).

Whatever that indicates about why Villa might be struggling at home, it’s clearly a problem and Emery, while positive about aspects of Villa’s play against the Black Cats, isn’t shying away from that.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

One place where his team don’t come up against the exact challenges posed by some of their Premier League opponents is in the Champions League, where Villa have won two home games out of two in the league phase this season. Indeed, European competitions underpin the very notion of Villa Park as a fortress under Emery, who took Villa back into Europe ahead of the 2023/24 season.

According to recent reports, their last home loss in Europe was against Olympiacos in that year’s Conference League semi-finals. They won five out of six at home in the Champions League the next season, drawing the other, and won all seven of their home matches in their successful Europa League campaign in 2025/26.

While the idea of Villa being strong at home has endured, the evidence of it in the Premier League has not.

Sources indicate that villa’s home results in the league might have been short of their expected levels since before the summer, but there are differences between this season and last. Simply selling Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Emiliano Martinez, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne and Ollie Watkins fundamentally changed the picture at Villa Park.

It has been revealed that rogers and Tielemans were important players for breaking games open. Villa significantly outscored their expected goals value in periods of last season and goals from outside the penalty area were key.

They don’t have the same superpower this season; improving their chance creation is a must and that’s not quick or easy with any group of players, never mind a newly assembled and young team.

While the idea of Villa being strong at home has endured, the evidence of it in the Premier League has not.

In a recent development, there’s also a looming, inconvenient possibility that’s beginning to sustain the weight of truth. Villa Park is a three-sided stadium this season because the North Stand – ordinarily full of home supporters – is being redeveloped behind one of the goals.

Industry observers note that the difference is intangible, indefinable, but it’s there. Even the players can’t quantify it because half of them have never played at a four-sided Villa Park, but the vacant structure behind the goal makes for an unusual atmosphere.

It has been revealed that emery has no interest in excuses. The Villa manager is focused on process and progress, taking every challenge for what it is and finding the answers to the questions they pose.

It has been revealed that the North Stand redevelopment won’t be accepted as mitigation for poor home form in the dugout any more than it will in the other three stands, but Emery is no fool. He accepted after the Sunderland draw that Villa Park and the team who call it home are missing ‘something’ without the North Stand. It’s not an excuse, just another test.

Villa need to pass that test. Home results have been a hallmark of the Emery era. The manager himself has qualified for Europe every season since long before he succeeded Steven Gerrard.

One win in six is a long way short of that standard. Emery’s meticulous and measured problem-solving has been called into action once more.

It has been revealed that chris is a Warwickshire-based freelance football writer specialising in West Midlands football, the Premier League, the EFL and the J.League. He is the author of the High Protein Beef Paste football newsletter and owner of Aston Villa Review. He supports Coventry Sphinx.

How to make climate anxiety your superpower

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 28 min read (5555 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~28 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that late last week the UN’s climate conference, COP31, failed to reach a consensus on its headline message.
  • I open up about my own climate anxiety and discover that there are still things that I can do to battle climate change.
  • Net zero emissions won’t reverse climate change — some nations look to ‘net negative’.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Download the Nature Podcast 23 November 2026.

Industry observers note that late last week the UN’s climate conference, COP31, failed to reach a consensus on its headline message. That news came on the heels of the UN acknowledging that the 1.5 ˚C warming limit set out in Paris will be breached. So, it’s easy to feel anxious in a world where it seems that not enough is being done about climate change. But is it possible to overcome such anxiety or even use it?

In the final episode of Cooked? I open up about my own climate anxiety and discover that there are still things that I can do to battle climate change. And how those small individual actions could potentially lead to more systemic change.

00:00 Can I do anything about my climate anxiety?

04:43 What the science says about ‘ecoanxiety’.

11:35 Can individuals really do anything?

18:44 How we can create bigger change.

Net zero emissions won’t reverse climate change — some nations look to ‘net negative’.

The rise of eco-anxiety: scientists wake up to the mental-health toll of climate change.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Liverpool fans did not miss a beat. They never do. “Poch is at the wheel,” they goaded as this calamity unfolded. But at the wheel of what, a clown car? The look of thunder on Mauricio Pochettino’s face noted it all as he got off to the worst start of any Manchester United manager – or head coach – in 100 years.

Recent findings suggest that the Pochettino bandwagon rolled into town with the usual fanfare of a fresh era, new belief, new hope; and then the wheels came off, the doors collapsed and the engine exploded. The opening quarter of an hour really was that farcical.

Recent findings suggest that in that time, away to Liverpool of all places, they were 2-0 down, a player down – and down and out. If Pochettino had any uncertainty over the scale of the task ahead of him, there it was laid bare. Of course United had some mitigation. They played almost the entire game with 10 men, but teams have coped with that before and shown far more resistance and resilience. By the time United did that, it was game over. No one expected a quick fix, but come on.

Any regrets, Mauricio? Whatever the salary, he could be forgiven for having a few as he watched on. This is a far cry from being in charge of the United States and watching them roll over Haiti 8-0 on aggregate, as he did last week. If Liverpool had been more ruthless, it could have been 8-0 here.

It has been revealed that in the end it was 4-0 – the same scoreline by which Lal Hilditch lost his first game at United, away to Bolton Wanderers in October 1926. Hilditch was a stop-gap player-manager and former central defender Pochettino may well have been tempted to bring himself on, even at the age of 54. He could barely have done worse.

Pochettino, too, can take some responsibility. Eyebrows were certainly raised when he dropped Harry Maguire – who he then had to bring on after 22 minutes – to hand Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in 357 days. De Ligt was then at fault for the first and, arguably, the second goal.

Recent findings suggest that did the head coach start with a back three or a back four? The players seemed confused. It eventually ended up as a back five.

In a recent development, but this was a collective failing for United. From the top – with director of football Jason Wilcox caught on camera with his head buried in his coat – through the club and out on the pitch. Pochettino is major on building a culture. So he has to abolish the comedy and the chaos and restore credibility.

United are deep in a relegation battle. Have no doubt. Eight points after 11 games means they are right now on target for fewer than 28 points, which is a lower points-per-game total than when they were relegated in 1974.

In a recent development, the work needed at United is monumental. The transfer strategy has been inexplicable, with the decision being to rebuild the attack last year, the midfield this summer and wait until next year to remodel the defence. The folly of that has been exposed by the fact that United have conceded 34 goals already this season, the most in the top five European leagues.

Industry observers note that united will argue, with justification, that Leny Yoro’s eighth-minute sending-off for denial of a goalscoring opportunity was harsh given that Alexander Isak appeared to have already lost control of the ball. But what was Yoro thinking as he bundled into the back of the forward? And what was De Ligt doing as he watched on, or lumbered on, after failing to track the run from Ronald Araújo’s ball over the top?

Andoni Iraola had a very clear message for his players ahead of this game: don’t fall into a trap.

It’s remarkable to see Manchester United arrive at Anfield in the bottom three but, to go back to that old cliche, the league table will mean nothing when the game begins and Liverpool’s Head Coach knows it only too well.

There will come a point when United leave their desperate form behind and Iraola, who could do with winning this contest after high-profile defeats to Arsenal and Manchester City, Isn’t being kidded by results after 10 games.

“United finished third in the table last season,” Iraola pointed out. “You are looking at a squad with exactly the same players. They had very, very good results, especially in the second half of the season. Now we have just started, this is just 10 games. So, for sure, they will be a lot higher in the table (soon). We have to rate them like this and the truth is the reference we have is that they finished third.”.

The key to success for Liverpool will be winning the midfield battle and Dominik Szoboszlai - whose form has been up and down - needs to recapture his best.

It is ironic that in their latest attempt to rejuvenate and restore some of their old fire, Manchester United have turned to a manager whose career needs a similar reawakening.

Pochettino can be even more grateful that a club of United’s stature have turned to him in their moment of need.

Bruno Fernandes indicates he has shelved talks over a fresh contract because it is not the “right moment” for discussions over his future as Manchester United captain.

Fernandes, 32, is out of contract next summer although United have a 12-month option to extend his deal to 2028.

The Portugal midfielder is understood to have rejected two contract offers from United since the summer but stated all his focus needs to be on trying to help the team out of their current plight.

United head into Sunday’s game against Liverpool at Anfield second from bottom in the Premier League.

“We spoke about the contract at the end of last season,” Fernandes told Sky Sports.

“We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.

“The most key thing now is that the club gets back to winning games.”.

According to recent reports, fernandes said claims he wants more money or a longer-term deal on offer are incorrect and that if finances were the concern he would have left Old Trafford before now. The captain has previously rejected lucrative offers from Saudi Arabia.

“The club offered me a fresh contract, so I think that, from their side, indicates that they want me to stay,” he said.

Sources indicate that “There’s no negotiations ongoing, but I’ve seen people saying that ‘He’s asked for more money, he’s asked for more years’. If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here.

“I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

“Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here.

Recent findings suggest that “The thing is, I’ve always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club. And I always said, in the moment the club thinks it’s time for me to move on, I will move on.

According to recent reports, “I’m not going to be the player that I’ve seen many in this time at Manchester United. They’re going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club says, ‘Bruno, it’s time to part ways’, I’m going to be the first one walking out the door.”.

United chief executive Omar Berrada said of Fernandes on Friday that it was “true that we’re having conversations about his latest contract” but that the club preferred “to keep that private”.

Having been voted PFA Player of the Year last season, Fernandes’ form has dropped off this term like that of the team.

He was dropped for the 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth in the wake of a 4-1 drubbing by Como when he criticised the tactics and approach of then head coach Michael Carrick.

Mauricio Pochettino, Carrick’s successor, confirmed on Friday that Fernandes would remain as captain.

Fernandes stated the United fans had been “far too patient with us” and hopes Pochettino - who wanted to bring the Portuguese to Spurs in 2019 - will bring a fresh energy.

“He’s someone that likes to bring a very good energy to the team, someone very positive, very strong, strict, remarked it straight away that he won’t allow us to not give him what he demands from the team, from each player,” Fernandes said.

“He wants the club to succeed so much, he wants to win games, and that’s pretty clear and obvious by the way he and his staff speak and want us to improve.

“Obviously [in 2019] I was a very young player that was eager to come to the Premier League. They had [Harry] Kane there, they had Dele Alli, Son, the chance of playing with those players in front was very attractive.”.

Recent findings suggest that pochettino arrived in the country on Wednesday after his final matches in charge of the US national team. He has inherited a squad with some players who have publicly criticised their own coach and technical director this season during their slide down the table.

The new United head coach, who has a contract until 2029, mentioned “culture” seven times in his first club interview in a pointed analysis of the work he needs to do at Old Trafford, starting with this weekend’s match against Liverpool at Anfield.

“The culture, to create the culture is the most important,” Pochettino noted. “To have the culture is the most important. Create the habit, the principle and I think that is what we want to create. We need to look forward and to find a way to create the best habit and the culture that makes us to be close to win every single game.”.

#94276. HENRY WINTER: Bruno Fernandes has been a brilliant servant, but it's time to cut the cord at Manchester United

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (889 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Fourfourtwo ↗ Open Full Page

HENRY WINTER: Bruno Fernandes has been a brilliant servant, but it's time to cut the cord at Manchester United

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (889 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fourfourtwo

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United are under latest management and need to be under new leadership on the field.
  • Industry observers note that bruno Fernandes has undeniably been a flickering beacon of brief hope for United in darkening times.
  • Recent findings suggest that even taking up the year’s option (unless to increase the player’s transfer fee) would be a retrograde step.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United are under latest management and need to be under new leadership on the field.

Industry observers note that bruno Fernandes has undeniably been a flickering beacon of brief hope for United in darkening times. He’s been their Player of the Year in five of the last seven seasons, risen to 19th of their greatest scorers with 113 goals, has scored 75 times (24 pens, four free-kicks) and provided 74 assists in 240 Premier League games and is the reigning Footballer of the Year. But it’s undeniably time for the club to face reality, resist the urge to extend a contract which expires next summer and build for the future.

Recent findings suggest that even taking up the year’s option (unless to increase the player’s transfer fee) would be a retrograde step. Fernandes is 32, slowing up, and not now “best in class, 10 out of 10s” to borrow Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s catchphrase. He is not the most convincing of captains, moans too much and flaps his arms like a fledgling dove attempting to leave the nest.

Fernandes would never, ever be considered one of United’s elite captains in a strong, historic field that includes Sir Bobby Charlton, Roy Keane, Bryan Robson, Steve Bruce, Roger Byrne, Nemanja Vidic and Gary Neville, amongst others.

All are different; Neville was very vocal, Charlton led by example, but were united in their total commitment.

Fernandes’ leadership qualities were brought into question when he openly criticised the tactics of Michael Carrick, effectively undermining him. That may not have been Fernandes’ intention when questioning the tactical approach against Como but it certainly didn’t help Carrick at a time when he needed players standing up to be counted, not standing up to his tactics in public. Such concerns – some of them legitimate – should have been aired in private.

Industry observers note that it highlighted a lack of leadership from Fernandes, a lack of gratitude, too. Fernandes wouldn’t have been named the writers’ Footballer of the Year and the players’ Player of the Year without Carrick reviving United’s fortunes and their No. 8’s form last season.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

In receiving the writers’ award in May, Fernandes eulogised about the interim head coach, praising “the amazing job” he did in guiding United into the Champions League and saying Carrick possesses the “great character to become a top manager”.

Such an endorsement from such an influential figure at the club, effectively the voice of the dressing-room, undoubtedly contributed to Ineos and the Glazers appointing Carrick to the permanent role.

Bruno’s voice is powerful. That is why it was damaging when he spoke out against Carrick’s tactics. “Lies,” was Bruno’s reaction to some of the interpretation of his words but mud stuck.

It has been revealed that carrick questioned individuals’ running stats – without naming Fernandes – and then dropped him for the game against Bournemouth. United need real leaders. In fairness to Fernandes, there are plenty of stories of the good work he does behind the scenes.

Who would inherit the armband in the unlikely event that Carrick’s successor, Mauricio Pochettino, was brave and looked to the future? Matthijs de Ligt, an Ajax captain at 18, would be a strong contender were it not for his back problems. Senne Lammens represents United admirably on and off the field, and was one of only two who emerged with reputation intact from Anfield.

The other was Kobbie Mainoo. It might seem a leap of faith in one so young, still only 21, but Mainoo could perform the duties until a more experienced leader was recruited by the club that once bought Keane, Bruce, Vidic etc. (All of this is a reminder of United’s need to buy leaders, powerful characters as well as good players).

According to recent reports, mainoo’s one of the few deserving of his place currently. He’s also an academy graduate, a local lad, and a link to great home-grown generations. Fans would love that re-affirmation of United’s identity. It would be quite a statement by Pochettino.

Recent findings suggest that mainoo has only minimal captaincy experience against Bayern Munich in 2017 (as a kid) and successfully with England Under-19s in 2023. More recently, more pertinently, Mainoo acted like a leader against Roma on November 3 when others were losing their discipline.

Recent findings suggest that it’s still too early, of course, and Mainoo is still developing but he could do the honours on a temporary basis in the unlikely event that United cut the cord with Fernandes. But a recruitment department incapable of making strong decisions and buying “best in class” – they were not in the running when Elliot Anderson and Morgan Rogers were available in the summer - may be tempted to go for the easy option of keeping Fernandes, rather than step into a new era.

Henry Winter is one of football's most popular and respected writers. Previously the Chief Football Writer for The Times and a Football Correspondent for The Daily Telegraph, his work now primarily features on his Substack. He has also lauched his own podcast 'The Winter View'.

Industry News: The best European strikers this century - ranked by you

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2088 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Classic number nines, penalty-box poachers, troublesome targetmen and tireless all-rounders.
  • There is no one-size fits all when it comes to determining great strikers, but they do all share a common trait - a ruthlessness in front of goal.
  • This week, however, we put the power in your hands to decide the best European frontmen of the 21st century.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The top 10 European strikers of the 21st century.

Classic number nines, penalty-box poachers, troublesome targetmen and tireless all-rounders.

There is no one-size fits all when it comes to determining great strikers, but they do all share a common trait - a ruthlessness in front of goal.

This week, however, we put the power in your hands to decide the best European frontmen of the 21st century.

Tens of thousands of you voted on the 20-man shortlist drawn up by our panel.

We then asked European football experts Guillem Balague, Julien Laurens and Raphael Honigstein to discuss your choices on the Euro Leagues podcast.

So from 10-1, here are the best European strikers this century - as voted for by you.

Top 10 European Strikers of the Century - Part One.

Karim Benzema comes in at number 10, the former Lyon and Real Madrid frontman's closest challengers coming from across the continent in the shape of Raul, Robin van Persie, Michael Owen and Miroslav Klose.

Industry observers note that laurens: "From a young age you could see he was something special. I know it was difficult at the beginning at Real Madrid, but in the post-Cristiano era he carried that team, wore the armband and won massive titles and trophies by being decisive in big moments. Like I used to say 'Karim the dream'.".

Industry observers note that honigstein: "The selflessness, the ability to work for the team. A sense of elegance and humility on the pitch, which is unusual in a goalscorer. I think he is unusual in that list. I think not many will define themselves through their teamwork and assists as much as their goals, but he was that player.".

Ruud van Nistelrooy edges Benzema, with whom he briefly overlapped at Real Madrid - the Dutchman teed up the Frenchman and scored himself in their only La Liga appearance together, before he left for Hamburg in January 2010 following injury problems.

The former PSV striker's most consistent spell, of course, came at Manchester United, where he scored 150 goals.

Honigstein: "He is the nicest guy but he never came across that way on the pitch. Typical trait of a striker, he would kill to score the goal. I think anyone who has grown up with him scoring goals, for United especially, must have a soft spot for him because he was a phenomenal poacher.".

Laurens: "He was a strong player physically, and despite the lack of pace the awareness in the box was just very special even with all the injuries.".

Zlatan Ibrahimovic slots in at eight, comfortably clear of Van Nistelrooy and Benzema. The Swede netted more than 500 times in a career that spanned Malmo, Ajax, Juventus, both Milans, Barcelona, Paris St-Germain, Manchester United and LA Galaxy.

Balague: "He was a big-game player and that explains the league titles with PSG. Scoring four goals against England, the overhead kick. The personality thing has put him one or two places in this list, saying 'I am great, I am the best'. If you keep saying you're great it makes people stop and think.".

Laurens: "The mentality of really believing he was the best and nobody was better than him, apart from maybe Brazilian Ronaldo, who was his idol growing up, and he would watch videos of him and try to replicate in his council estate. If you watch a highlight reel of his best goals he was incredible.".

Honigstein: "What makes him unique among the strikers is his technique, You could see elements of martial arts in his goals. No-one scores goals like that.".

The first Englishman on the list, although the third to have represented Manchester United - it's the Old Trafford outfit's record goalscorer, Wayne Rooney.

Sources indicate that honigstein: "I don't think there is anyone who would've watched English football at that time [early in his career] and not been enthralled by his game. The only downside is the combination of injuries and not the most professional lifestyle meant he did not fulfil his potential. He could've been Messi.".

In a recent development, balague: "What could have been, yes. He was the national team's record scorer too before Harry Kane took it. I find him to deserve this place as he had to adapt to a lot of strikers and he did it well. He had the ability to link up and score. He was very intelligent.".

Laurens: "He is the most street footballer England has ever seen. There's no rules, that kind of anger you saw on the pitch. I don't think people in England realise how good he was.".

According to recent reports, what does becoming the all-time World Cup top goalscorer get you? Sixth place on the best European strikers this century list. The Real Madrid forward, 27, just misses out on the top five.

Laurens: "Maybe if we do this ranking again in a few years he will be higher. I would have had him top five, for sure. He has scored more than 400 goals. I don't think Messi and Ronaldo had scored that many at that age, so he's ahead. I don't know if he will play for as long as them but he hasn't done much wrong in his career.".

It has been revealed that balague: "This list has to do what you feel about the player, not science - 22 goals in 22 appearances in World Cups and [Euro] Championships. He should be at least top three because of that. Great stats, but we're not in love with him.".

Recent findings suggest that honigstein: "I don't think there is a forward that is as good as footballer as him in 2026. On that basis alone he should be higher, but people when they vote have other things in their head. The only way to win everyone over is to score more goals and win more World Cups for France, which I think is possible.".

There was little between Mbappe and Erling Haaland, but it is Manchester City's prolific Norwegian who slips in at fifth. The 26-year-old has already scored more than 300 club goals and has a staggering 68 in 61 games for his country.

Balague: "Mbappe should be higher than him. Haaland scored 52 goals in 53 games [in 2022-23], that is astonishing, but he's gone 11 finals without scoring. We're talking about the best. We're talking about what we see at the moment and what we see is someone who is calculated but in a more charming way. An ability to score we haven't seen in a while; power, ability to finish. He is not world class to the level of others.".

Industry observers note that honigstein: "I don't think it's fair to judge him on just that. They [Manchester City] won the Champions League when he was there. When Haaland arrived with Pep Guardiola, they found a way to do it. What makes him unique is the physical attributes and the pace. To have both is unique. He can sprint like a 100m sprinter. Is he the fifth best striker of the 21st Century? I don't think he's that far behind.".

Interesting, this, because Robert Lewandowski is well clear of Haaland in fourth, but the leap from the Polish forward to the top three is massive - more than 10,000 votes.

The 38-year-old is still chipping away for Chicago Fire in Major League Soccer, having been a reliably ruthless assassin for Barcelona, Bayern and Dortmund.

Honigstein: "He used to play basketball, judo, handball - his father wanted him to have a wholesome education. You could see his completeness that he had as a centre-forward. Nothing in his game was extraordinary but in terms of ticking all the boxes, none come close to him.".

Recent findings suggest that balague: "He said he learned to be an elite striker when he forgot what he had just done, like a fish. Mistakes he had in his head affected his performance. One day he just continued like it didn't matter.".

Laurens: "He won the Ballon d'Or in Covid, it won't be on his mantlepiece but we all know it was his.".

Fresh from his Ballon d'Or triumph, England's record goalscorer and appearance maker rides into the top three on the back of 61 goals in 51 outings for Bayern Munich last season.

Kane left the Premier League three years ago with the second-most goals ever in the competition, and is also Tottenham's all-time record scorer.

It has been revealed that honigstein: "Third place, at least. He is doing incredible things. At 33, still not quite at his peak. I don't think he relies on his pace, physicality, it's all about intelligence, technique. I don't think there's anyone in the game that strikes a ball as well as him right now. I don't think any player comes close that we've talked about so far in overall work-rate, defending, helping the team, making tackles in your box in the 90th minute when you're 3-0 up because he's that kind of guy. He is humble and a superb human being.".

Recent findings suggest that laurens: "What I love about Kane, from a young age, a lot of this list you just knew the trajectory would be all the way to the top. Kane was not like that. It could have been very different for him. Nobody at 17 would've said he was going to win the Ballon d'Or. Nobody believed in him like the others. Kane had a very different journey.".

It has been revealed that runner-up Thierry Henry is the only striker in the top six who is retired. A World Cup and Euros winner with France, Henry won titles with Arsenal - where he scored 228 goals - and a Champions League with Barcelona.

Honigstein: "During his time, I don't think there was a player like him in the Premier League. The way he played football was stylish, elegant, but there was almost a kind of a romantic connection between him and the ball. I don't think there was anyone near that kind of level of technique and, for want of a better word, va-va-voom he exuded. That just made for amazing viewing.".

According to recent reports, laurens: "For me as a fellow Parisien, he's a very special player, a very special man. A career that has been incredible from a young age. It's that season in the Premier League - 24 goals, 20 assists in 38 games - not even Kane or Benzema or Cristiano, OK, Messi is different, but they haven't done that and yet he did it.

"There are still some people who undervalue him and underappreciate him and the monster that he was on the football pitch. He had it all. The pace, the style, the elegance, the technique, the mentality, the goals, the aura, the charisma. Just everything you wanted if you were to build a striker. One of the greatest football brains ever.".

Sources indicate that of course, at number one, it's the man chasing the 1,000-goal dream. Cristiano Ronaldo may have retired from Portugal duty with 146 notches on his strike chart but the quest goes on at Al-Nassr.

The 41-year-old's evolution from tricky winger to prolific frontman has taken him from Sporting to Manchester United, twice, Real Madrid, Juventus and now Saudi Arabia.

Recent findings suggest that balague: "He's the best striker in history. His numbers are incredible. He won't stop until he gets to 1,000. He is somebody who is special. We know his background, how he wanted to be Ballon d'Or winner at 12 and didn't stop until he got there. He ran up the mountains of Funchal with weights in his ankles and snuck into the gym when it was closed to get the physique he wanted.".

Laurens: "Always in the right place at the right time. The instinct. He was born with a gift, like all in this list. But you still have to work hard. Nobody will ever reach those levels again. 1,000 goals for club and country will never be done again, I think.".

Honigstein: "Peak Ronaldo for me was Gareth Bale scoring and him looking very unhappy. I don't think there will be any dispute about him being the greatest. Somebody who has done it all, won it all, and he's still going for the love of it.".

Jack Grealish has returned to the Everton squad for the first time since being dropped for a breach of discipline.

Grealish last played in a 2-0 home defeat to Chelsea on 17 October, with the former England international punished for skipping training when he was not authorised to do so before the Carabao Cup tie with Newcastle.

He has not featured in four games - the first of which, against Arsenal, due to illness - with manager David Moyes not including him in previous matchday squads due to a lack of match fitness.

But after featuring in a behind-closed-doors friendly against Derby during the international break, Grealish has returned to the first-team fold and starts on the bench for Everton’s trip to Brentford on Monday night.

Moyes has preferred Merlin Rohl, Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Tyrique George in the attacking midfield positions behind Thierno Barry, but Grealish could be in line for a substitute cameo.

Grealish apologised to fans after his friendly return to action, writing on his Instagram story: "Nice to be back out there with the boys today after a few good days training.

"I want to apologise to the fans and everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks.

According to recent reports, "I love playing for this club and can’t wait to be back playing in front of you guys in an Everton shirt. See you all soon.".

Grealish spent the 2025-26 season on loan at Everton before injury disrupted his spell, but he secured another temporary deal on transfer deadline day.

In his absence, Everton have won three of their last four matches to move up to sixth in the Premier League table, while also earning their spot in the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup.

Breaking: Chemistry giant George Whitesides dies: one of the most influential researchers of his generation

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, george Whitesides, a towering figure in chemistry who pushed chemists to cross boundaries to solve global problems, died on 19 November.
  • His son George, a US congressman representing California, unveiled Whitesides’s passing on the social media platform X, saying that the chemist died at home surrounded by family.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

George Whitesides at Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts, where he spent most of his academic career.Credit: Rick Friedman/Corbis via Getty.

In a recent development, george Whitesides, a towering figure in chemistry who pushed chemists to cross boundaries to solve global problems, died on 19 November. He was 87.

His son George, a US congressman representing California, unveiled Whitesides’s passing on the social media platform X, saying that the chemist died at home surrounded by family.

Meet the soft, cuddly robots of the future.

Meet the soft, cuddly robots of the future.

Industry observers note that whitesides made landmark contributions to many fields: he was a pioneer in patterning surfaces with molecules, a technique that enabled ‘lab on a chip’ diagnostic devices, advances in nanotechnology and more. He prided himself on switching research interests often, telling students, “If somebody else is working on something, don’t work on it.”.

Recent findings suggest that following the news of the chemist’s passing, messages celebrating his impact flooded online platforms. “I am so saddened to hear of his passing,” Zhenan Bao, a chemical engineer at Stanford University in California, wrote on LinkedIn. “George highlighted us that the most important problems don’t respect the lines between disciplines. He moved freely across chemistry, materials, biology, and engineering.”.

Whitesides trained hundreds of scientists who came through his laboratory, first at Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and then at Harvard University, both in Cambridge. But he also inspired many others, says Joseph DeSimone, a polymer scientist at Stanford. In traditional chemistry departments, “there’s often a lot of pressure to stay in your lane, and he made it okay not to. In fact, he made it exciting not to”, DeSimone says.

Whitesides was born in Louisville, Kentucky, in 1939. One of his first experiences with chemistry was as a teenager, cleaning glassware at his father’s chemical engineering firm in his hometown.

After a bachelor’s degree in chemistry at Harvard, he enroled for a PhD at California Institute of Technology in Pasadena, studying how the workhorse chemicals known as Grignard reagents form and behave.

By 1963, Whitesides became a faculty member at MIT, where he would switch to studying the fundamentals of self-assembled monolayers (SAMs)1. These are tightly packed coatings of organic compounds that are a single-molecule thick, formed spontaneously because of forces drawing the molecules to a surface and to one another.

George Whitesides and his research group pioneered low-cost, paper-based microfluidic 'lab-on-a-chip' devices. Credit: Volker Steger/Science Photo Library.

From there, Whitesides saw ways of using SAMs to easily and cheaply create patterned surfaces — which at the time were often made with complicated lithography techniques involving light and ‘stencils’. He would go on to invent soft lithography2, which instead uses polymer stamps to transfer micro- and nanoscopic patterns of molecules to surfaces.

Industry observers note that this became an “enabling” research tool, says John Rogers, a materials scientist at Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois, who was a postdoc with Whitesides at Harvard. The ability to easily pattern surfaces opened the door to creating 3D nanostructures, microfluidics and much more. It also “democratized” the ability to do this type of research, Rogers adds, because you no longer needed sophisticated cleanroom facilities and etching techniques to create such materials.

#94270. Latest Update: How Premier League's big six keep getting richer
