#94135. Breaking: On this day in space! Nov. 19, 2005: Japan's Hayabusa spacecraft makes 1st-ever liftoff from surface of an asteroid

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (795 w)

Breaking: On this day in space! Nov. 19, 2005: Japan's Hayabusa spacecraft makes 1st-ever liftoff from surface of an asteroid

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (795 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • 19, 2005, the Japanese Hayabusa spacecraft made the first liftoff from an asteroid.
  • Asteroids are space rocks that were formed during the early solar system.
  • Hayabusa's sample return capsule returned to Earth in June 2010.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Nov. 19, 2005, the Japanese Hayabusa spacecraft made the first liftoff from an asteroid. Hayabusa was supposed to return asteroid samples to Earth.

Asteroids are space rocks that were formed during the early solar system. We study asteroids to learn more about the solar system's history. Hayabusa (pronounced HI-uh-BOOS-uh) made two touchdowns on asteroid Itokawa (EE -toh-KA-wah). Each time, the spacecraft went into safe mode. Controllers weren't sure if Hayabusa gathered any material. But they sent the spacecraft back to Earth anyway.

Hayabusa's sample return capsule returned to Earth in June 2010. Scientists found dust of Itokawa inside the capsule, proving that it did indeed capture samples of Itokawa.

The primary goal of Japan's Hayabusa mission to asteroid Itokawa was never to be the first spacecraft to liftoff from a space rock. The mission was always aimed at collecting samples from an asteroid and returning them to Earth.

In a recent development, it was a hard road to Itokawa for Hayabusa. The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) debuted the probe on May 9, 2003, with plans for an arrival at the asteroid in the early summer of 2005.

That asteroid arrival was delayed until September 2005 after a solar storm degraded Hayabusa's solar arrays, limiting the available power for its ion engines.

Still, Hayabusa managed to limp along its path to reach the asteroid Itokawa on Sept. 12, 2005.

Sources indicate that hayabusa dropped a small lander onto Itokawa, but that probe was apparently lost. Hayabusa then dropped a landing target on the asteroid, and ultimately managed to touchdown about 99 feet from the marker, JAXA has said.

It has been revealed that during its first landing on Nov. 19, Hayabusa descended to a point just 56 feet above Itokawa before going silent for 3 hours, according to an Associated Press report. Once contact was restored, JAXA officials confirmed the probe had landed, and it eventually lifted off for a second attempt. That was the first-ever liftoff from an asteroid by a spacecraft.

"The spacecraft actually bounced off the surface a few times and spent about 39 minutes resting on the asteroid, but apparently the samplers never fired," Andrew Cheng, a Hayabusa science team member at Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory, told Space.com at the time. There was hope that some material managed to make it inside the collector anyway.

"After all the thrashing about ... there is no way to confirm that," Cheng had mentioned. The second landing on Itokawa occured a few days later on Nov. 26, 2005.

In November 2010, five months after Hayabusa's sample-return capsule touched down in Australia, JAXA declared some good news: Hayabusa did collect 1,500 dust grains from asteroid Itokawa, samples that were jammed into the collector by the two landings, despite is collector mechanism not firing.

The ultimate success of Hayabusa spurred the creation of another sample-return mission by Japan: Hayabusa2.

Industry observers note that that probe rolled out in December 2014 and arrived at asteroid Ryugu (REE-ooh-goo) in 2018. It collected its own samples and returned them to Earth in December 2020. The Hayabusa2 probe is now on an extended mission to the asteroid 2015 BM510, which it will fly by in April 2028. It had planned to land on a strange asteroid 1998 KY26, but suffered engine trouble that made that rendezvous impossible.

As an editor with over 10 years of experience in science journalism she has previously written for Scholastic Classroom Magazines, MedPage Today and The Joint Institute for Computational Sciences at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. After studying physics at the University of Tennessee in her hometown of Knoxville, she earned her graduate degree in Science, Health and Environmental Reporting (SHERP) from Newly introduced York University. Hanneke joined the Space.com team in 2016 as a staff writer and producer, covering topics including spaceflight and astronomy. She currently lives in Seattle, home of the Space Needle, with her cat and two snakes. In her spare time, Hanneke enjoys exploring the Rocky Mountains, basking in nature and looking for dark skies to gaze at the cosmos.

For Bo Derek, it's all about love.

The Bolero actress revealed the secret to making her relationship with husband John Corbett with after over two decades together.

Ultimately, though, it's Corbett's presence in her life that is the biggest gift of all.

In a recent development, "He keeps me laughing," Derek said. "He’s very youthful, enthusiastic.".

While the couple occasionally hosts a couple of friends for small dinner parties at their 110-acre ranch near Santa Barbara, Calif., they tend to prefer spending time at home with one another and their two German Shepherds.

In a recent development, "When we first met, he didn’t want to have a girlfriend with a dog because they just require too much time," Derek shared. "You’re just off going off having fun, and you got to rush back to the dog. And now I can’t get him to go anywhere with me because he doesn’t want to leave the dogs.".

Keep reading for more celeb couples who have shared the secrets to their long-lasting relationships...

Mariska Hargitay & Peter Hermann.

It has been revealed that "I never thought that I would laugh this much in my marriage. That is such a fundamental ingredient of who you are, this insistence on joy," Hermann detailed to his bride of their partnership of over 20 years in Marlo Thomas and Phil Donahue's 2020 book What Makes a Marriage Last. "And I think what sustains our marriage is that I know you love me in spite of who I am, and that is the definition of grace."Seeking out that happiness is key. Even after a particularly robust argument, "One of us will test the waters with a joke—about the very thing we were fighting about," Herman shared of life with the Law & Order: SVU star. "It's like one of us indicates, 'I'm not saying I was wrong, and I'm not still insisting I was entirely right, but can we at least inch our way back toward the place where we caught at stuff together?' Once that happens, it's a pretty good sign that things are on their way to getting patched up.".

Sources indicate that they've avoided need for any major renovation by sticking to the same advice they got in premarital counseling ahead of their 2003 vows. Even five kids in, Tuesday date nights are a must and they've held off on purchasing a TV, instead finding other ways to connect. But if Chip were to offer any tip to follow, it'd be to pursue the person you love "like a hornet." Some two decades in, he stated, he still feels like the guy hoping to get a second date. "I'm not saying she'd never cheat on me," he explained, "but it's not going to be because I never told her I loved her or because I didn't send her flowers or I forgot our anniversary.".

Sources indicate that "My first piece of advice is not to take advice from celebrities," Bacon joked of his 36-year union. It's as succinct as their other go-to, "Keep the fights clean and the sex dirty," a phrase developed specifically to end any further chatter about their marriage. Truthfully, though, they make it a point not to let arguments linger, rarely digging in for the sake of the victory. "Honestly, we don't like to fight, so when we actually are in an argument, we're both looking for a solution," The Closer actress explained to Thomas and Donahue. "For the most part we're struggling to get back to everything being okay, because it sucks to fight." Because, when it comes down to it, she continued, "There is no Plan B. No matter what, we want to work it out.".

According to recent reports, over 37 years into marriage, the actors have mastered the art of fighting fair. "Tracy and I don't pick scabs," explained the Family Ties alum. "In some marriages, people look at their partner and see vulnerability and they just can't help but go after that vulnerability, like it's a sport or something. We don't do that." That's not to say they don't have arguments. "If I've mentioned something stupid, I have the tendency to want to take it back and make it all okay," he said. "But that doesn't really work." Instead, he follows her lead and tries to give her space. She, in turn, offers up understanding: "Sometimes you just have to say to yourself, 'You know what? He said something schmucky and it made me feel bad. But he's a good person and I'm going to give him the benefit of the doubt that he didn't realize that what he said hurt my feelings.'".

It has been revealed that "He still makes me laugh more than any human being," Curtis said about the Waiting for Guffman director on Today in December 2024, ahead of the couple's 40th wedding anniversary, adding jokingly, "and I'm sure there's something about me that he likes. I don't know what it is, but I'm sure there's something.".

Neil Patrick Harris & David Burtka.

"I think one of the things that has kept us together all of these years is that we both define relationships as something that's relatively indefinable," the How I Met Your Mother alum said. Through 21 years of career shifts (actor-chef Burtka released his cookbook Life Is a Party in 2019), parenting twins Gideon and Harper and dealing with tough times, "Marriage never stays the same," explained Harris. "When you have sex with the same person over and over, it gets redundant, and so you try different things. Then one day you don't like each other, and suddenly you're not attracted to each other, so you have to figure out how to be reattracted to them—but in a different way because you're aging."Eventually, he continued, you find yourself more attracted to their soul. And then their body again. "It all keeps morphing," he noted. "So in a weird way, we keep falling in love with each other in different ways, over and over.".

Appropriately, the comic actors believe their funniness gives them life. And not just in their 19-year union itself. "Whenever we have a good laugh," noted the Can You Ever Forgive Me? actress, "especially a crazy one, when you're like, Oh, my God, and you're almost dizzy—we always assign it a specific amount of time that it added to our lives. And I'm always adding it up. I'll say, 'Okay, that was like two months—I just got two more months to live!'"They put a time limit on disagreements as well. Citing the oft-repeated don't go to bed angry rule, Falcone, remarked, "I tried it once, and I realized that in the morning I had forgotten what I was mad about. You're not getting any answers if you're parsing out an argument when everybody is tired and possibly had a drink or two. I've never had the thing where you're having an argument at ten o'clock at night, and then you say, 'Well, that was good. I'm glad we got to the bottom of that. We agree. Truce signed.'".

Each having wed before they found their way to the other in 1995, they not only had to navigate a marriage, but life as step-parents to two children apiece. "There is no book that tells you how to do it, so the one thing I figured out right away is that they already have a mom—and it's not me. So what did they need from me?" the Zoey's Extraordinary Playlist actor recalled. "That's when I realized that everybody needs a cheerleader, right? There's never too many of those in your life, so that's what I'll be. I never set their boundaries, disciplined them, or tried to teach them right from wrong. They have parents who do that."The Cheers alum agreed with her stance wholeheartedly. "I think that's really wise, to offer yourself as a friend," he stated. "‘I'm not going to discipline you and I'm not going to judge you. What I'm going to do is hang out with you and be there for you.' And that's what you have to do: absolutely, genuinely be there.".

The moment same-sex civil unions were legalized in Britain, the music icon and the Canadian ad exec were joined together in a Dec. 21, 2005 ceremony. They repeated the process on the exact same day nine years later once they were able to legally wed. And yet the anniversary they recognize is their unexpected meeting during a 1993 weekend dinner party at the singer's Windsor, England flat, his friend having set the guest list.Every Saturday, no matter where they are in the world, together or apart, the two pen a handwritten note to each other, by the authors' count, some 1,352 letters in all. "There's something very spiritual and real about handwriting," explains Furnish, "and the cards are a chance to reflect on the week that's passed and talk about the week that's coming up." Agreed the five-time Grammy winner, "It's part of the success, I think, of a lasting relationship. Communication is the most important thing.".

Sources indicate that having literally Secreted their 40-year marriage into existence ("Six months before I met him, I had these recurring dreams about this person I was going to marry,") they make sure their union has remained front-and-center even as their entire existence has shifted. "Marriage is a priority for both of us. And that means that we act on that and refocus when we've lost sight of the ball," she stated. If the surgeon could prescribe one piece of advice, it would be to place that bond above all else. "The bottom line is this: I would do anything for her. Climb any mountain, take any bullet—in the chest, too, by the way. I might do things that justifiably make her really angry at me, but I would never let anything block me from delivering my love to her," he swore. If you appreciate how valuable marriage is to your long-term happiness, he continued, "You will never let anyone touch it.".

Industry observers note that ABC News reporter Roberts isn't always one for chit-chat. "I don't like the check-in," she explaind. "If you're calling just to say, 'So, what's up?' no, I do not like that." Everyone's favorite TV weatherman, however, is a phone guy. And after years of chafing against his frequent calls, a pal proposed something that changed her stance. "One friend remarked to me, 'Did you ever think that maybe he just feels comfortable when he hears your voice, because that tells him that all is right in the world?'" she recounted. "And I thought, 'That's very sweet. I'd never thought about it in that way. And if it means something to him, then it should mean something to me.'"Now, she said, "I have learned to take a breath and say, 'Sweetie, I've got some stuff going on, but what's going on with you? Great. I'm glad to hear from you. Got to go. Talk to you later. Love you.' That makes all the difference in the world to him, and it doesn't kill me for two minutes to be nice and sweet." They celebrated their 29th anniversary in September 2024.

According to recent reports, the building blocks for their nearly 30-year union began back in their newlywed days, when any fight—one involved the Riverdale actor throwing the talk show host's ring out the window—felt like it could be it. "Early in a marriage, it's easy to let little things become significant things—whether it's financial strain or career strain or you have kids and you're sleep-deprived," espoused the LIVE With Kelly and Ryan star. "But Mark taught me to walk away and take a breath. That's when you figure out that it's not a marriage-defining moment."Some hard-earned wisdom, to be sure, but now the parents of three are reaping the benefits. "Anytime you see a couple who seems truly happy, you can bet they've gone through some crazy, crazy stuff together and they've survived," he stated. "That's something to be proud of.".

In a recent development, she's an introvert, she mentioned, "maybe a step away from being a straight-up loner"; he's the ultimate extrovert "the mayor of everywhere," as he put it. She's a touch messy; he's "a little OCD" noted the Oscar winner. But, wed since 2003, they've long since learned to let the other do their thing. That's the advice the How to Get Away With Murder lead said she gives to all her soon-to-be-wed friends. "Marriage does not start when you walk down the aisle," she shared. "Your marriage starts when you look over at a person who you love more than anything, and there's something about him—just one character trait that makes you say to yourself, 'Oh man, that's going to drive me crazy. I don't know if I can deal with this.' And then the next minute you say, 'But you know what? I love him.' That's when your marriage starts.".

Industry observers note that you don't reach the 50-year mark in any relationship by letting disagreements drag on. Any time there's a blowup, noted the Grace and Frankie star, "Usually, I'm the one who apologizes. It's not hard because I love her and can't bear for her to feel lonely for even five minutes." Even better is when she can avoid saying she's sorry to the writer altogether. Her top takeaway, she shared, "Remember, when you're angry at your partner and say something hurtful, you will be more angry at yourself later for having noted hurtful things to the person you love. You'll feel angry twice. Not good for your blood pressure, and certainly not good for your relationship.".

Judges Judy Sheindlin & Jerry Sheindlin.

In a recent development, few things are more on brand than former Upcoming York State Supreme Court judge Jerry declaring their decades-long union works because he usually lets the Judge Judy icon win. But for his bride it's more about knowing you're not always going to like the final verdict. Their 12-year marriage dissolved in 1990 when he couldn't be the caretaker she needed following her father's death. Yet, when they got back together one year later and promptly remarried, she had no delusions that he was suddenly going to be the type to run the household or take the lead on birthday aims. "Every relationship is different, but there is a common thread of unhappiness, and that unhappiness comes from trying to make another person different from who they are. You can try, but they're always going to resent it," she explained matter-of-factly. "I don't think you should marry anyone with the expectation of changing who they are.".

The Lost alum would be, well, lost without his longtime love, who he married in 1993. As he explained to E! News in April 2025, "My wife—being patient as I traipse around the world, going from job to job—she's kept our family stable. She's been fantastic.".

Calling her a "very patient woman," the actor said his wife and their two sons keeps him "humble no matter what's happening.".

"They shape my values," he added. "It's great to have that perspective and North Star.".

Creators Choice Awards: Our favorite creators name their favorite tools

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2097 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The creator economy has exploded in recent years.
  • In a survey from The Conversation, more than 60 percent of middle and high school students remarked they wanted to be influencers or have a career based on what they saw online.
  • At Mashable, we’re constantly covering what’s happening in the creator world, whether that’s at VidCon, the TikTok Awards, or in conversations across the internet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The creator economy has exploded in recent years. TV shows feature creators doing cameos as themselves, your favorite author is probably on BookTok, and Starbucks is paying baristas to make creator-style videos.

In a survey from The Conversation, more than 60 percent of middle and high school students remarked they wanted to be influencers or have a career based on what they saw online.

At Mashable, we’re constantly covering what’s happening in the creator world, whether that’s at VidCon, the TikTok Awards, or in conversations across the internet. For our "Creator Playbook" series, we ask creators how they turn content into a career and about the tools they use to do so for "In My Bag.".

It has been revealed that in our inaugural Creators’ Choice Awards, we surveyed our favorite creators across the internet, including some of our Mashable 101 nominees. We wanted to know which gear and tools they use to see which brands and products are the most loved among digital creators. Now, we're ready to announce the winners.

Sources indicate that A smartphone is the most basic tool a creator holds in their toolkit. Not only does it act as the camera, microphone, editor, and uploader, but it's also how they connect with followers.

In our own reporting, Senior Reporter Haley Henschel wrote, "For most of us, our phone is the most important device we own," calling it a "lifeline to friends" and "our primary gateway to the internet." She also noted that unless you carry around a separate camera, your phone is also how you document the world.

Phones are where people create and consume content. So, of course, we wanted to ask creators which phone brands they use and love.

No surprise, our pool of creators overwhelmingly use Apple iPhones. They cited that they prefer Apple because the phones are easy to use and do everything they need from a mobile device. Most of our respondents had an iPhone 15 or newer.

“My entire life, business, and career [are] managed and created using my iPhone,” one respondent wrote.

Mashable's resident iPhone reviewer, Senior Editor Stan Schroeder, called all of the latest iPhones "blazing fast," and has lauded their cameras, battery life, and impressively fast performance in his reviews.

Some creators also commented on the phones’ long battery lives and impressive performance and features. One person mentioned, “This phone is a workhorse,” while another called their iPhone “a power performer” that “gets everything you need done with a snap, with excellent battery life and storage.”.

We know that Apple loyalty runs deep, so we suspected it would hold the top spot among our surveyed creators. One even called themself “a forever customer of the brand.”.

Samsung Galaxy phones were a second favorite among our creator pool. Samsung stood out for its cameras and overall satisfaction with its phones. Per our reporting, Samsung's Galaxy S26 Ultra is "faster than some mid-range laptops we've tried," and the brand makes the best foldable Android phone.

“It is the best phone available,” said one respondent who has a Samsung Galaxy S26+. Another creator agreed that “Samsung makes the best phones, period.”.

Survey respondents praised Samsung’s operating system, processor, AI integration, and long battery life.

“I do the majority of my content creation on my phone and find it very easy to use,” one creator said.

In a recent development, while a phone might be the most accessible or most-used tool for content creation, some creators take video editing or design work to their personal computers. Henschel writes, "The best laptops are fast enough for their primary use cases, well-made, and priced fairly for their specs." We were curious which machines power our favorite creators’ content, and the results were pretty split among different brands.

Though, our creators did choose laptop brands that Mashable experts personally recommend.

Apple reigned supreme as the most preferred laptop brand for our survey takers. They like MacBooks for their compatibility with other Apple devices, sleek design, and overall usability.

In a recent development, "It looks nice and it works for so many things," one respondent wrote. "There is nothing you can't do on it — it's definitely worth the price.".

Creators also reported that the software they use to create their content runs well on Apple laptops and that the MacBooks are fast.

Sources indicate that one creator wrote, “As a musician, I love the MacBook Pro because of its capabilities for creating music and music content. I frequently run Logic Pro and MuseScore on my MacBook to create music, both of which run super smoothly. I also use it to edit videos featuring my music for social media. I would definitely recommend this computer to another musician.”.

Another said their MacBook is “very capable” of doing what they need when putting together content.

Apple’s laptops are definitely a favorite for creatives. “It's great for everything you need as a content creator,” wrote one respondent.

Recent findings suggest that our creators also prefer Dell for their computing needs. Multiple people noted the longevity of their Dell laptops, with one noting that they’ve had theirs for more than 10 years.

Respondents mentioned simply, “I love my Dell,” and “It’s my favorite.”.

It has been revealed that other comments praised Dell’s processing speed, RAM capacity, battery life, ease of use, and durability. These same qualities are why you'll find multiple Dell computers on our list of the best Windows laptops.

Participants in our Creators’ Choice survey also preferred Microsoft laptops. They lauded the laptops' speed, processor, and design, with one person commenting specifically on how easy it is for them to create and edit vlogs.

One creator put it simply: “It's an all-rounder and is good for most people.”.

Sources indicate that the final winner in the laptop category is HP. Creators love the brand’s laptops for their speed, quality, and affordability.

“My HP laptop is fast, reliable, and handles everyday tasks with ease,” wrote one participant, adding that it’s actually a great value for its price.

Industry observers note that others noted HP’s ease in multitasking and the power behind its laptops. One creator stated, “It is easy to use, affordable, durable, and can be used for many things such as recording, video calls, and editing pictures.”.

While video is arguably the most popular medium for creators in 2026, many still use photo-editing tools and incorporate photography into their feeds.

Adobe reigns supreme in editing tools for our creators, including its photo-centric tools like Photoshop and Lightroom. Many respondents praised Adobe apps’ ease of use and their editing tools for both professionals and hobbyists.

Multiple people stated Adobe is their “go-to” editing tool and that it’s “the best I’ve ever used.”.

“This photo editing software is amazing, and I swear by it,” wrote a survey respondent. “The results speak for themselves.”.

One person mentioned that Adobe’s AI features “make editing so much more efficient” and that they’d recommend it based on that alone.

The second-most preferred photo editing tool among our survey pool is Canva. Creators love that it’s accessible and easy to use, even for non-professionals.

One comment stated, “I like that it's free to use and still has good editing tools for free customers.”.

Videos make up the majority of creator-made content on social media, whether on TikTok, Instagram Reels, or YouTube, and our creators have two favorite video editing brands.

Adobe was their top choice again, with a large number of responses noting how easy the programs are to use. One creator called Adobe Premiere “an amazing software,” while another stated it’s “perfect for what I need it for.”.

Others commented on Adobe being a great editing platform and having a good variety of editing tools.

Another favorite video editing tool among our creator pool is CapCut. The mobile-first editing program is incredibly easy to use, according to our respondents. They also like it for its TikTok integration.

One respondent who says they’ve been an avid CapCut user before it was even called CapCut wrote, “It’s been the best editing software I’ve ever used.”.

Affordability is another area where CapCut shines — one creator called it “a steal.”.

Graphic design can enhance your content with stronger visuals or allow you to create recognizable branding.

Sources indicate that and, once again, Adobe was a favorite for our creators. They prefer it for its ease of use and breadth of tools.

One creator stated Adobe has a “great comprehensive suite of design and editing tools that are crucial to making the best content.”.

Another called Adobe the “best in the business.”.

Industry observers note that canva was another top choice in our survey results. People prefer it because it’s also very easy to use and free or affordable.

“I like Canva because it has great tools that make editing more fun,” wrote one respondent.

Another said, “It can do lots of different things to make great products.”.

According to recent reports, though smartphones have pretty stellar onboard cameras, many creators still opt for a dedicated vlogging camera. You'll find an array of cameras featured in our In My Bag series, but these are the top three brands, according to the creators who took our survey.

Canon was the favorite camera brand among the survey pool. They praised Canon cameras’ great quality and durability. One person said their Canon PowerShot G7 X “has been a great camera that lasted through the years.”.

Sources indicate that creators from our survey also use and like Sony vlogging cameras. They recommend Sony cameras for beginners and pros alike. One respondent said, “I recommend them because they have very good quality; they are certainly very good investments.”.

Creators also like Panasonic for its audio quality, image quality, battery life, and user-friendliness.

According to recent reports, while we had creators answering questions about their favorite tools and gear, we, of course, also had to ask them about which social media platform they use the most. Drumroll please….

Facebook actually came out on top as the most-used social media among our respondents.

They like Facebook mostly for personal use and keeping up with friends and family members. Many people stated the platform is great for connecting with others.

“I have been using it for years and is the best way i have found to stay in touch with people and share my story,” noted one respondent.

Sources indicate that on the subject of using Facebook for years, one person called it “the O.G. of social media,” adding that “there is nothing not to like” about it.

Industry observers note that another Meta platform was also a favorite: Creators like Instagram for how easy it is to use and for connecting with friends and followers. According to one creator, “it offers a visually engaging platform to connect with friends, family, and global communities.”.

Others praised the creativity and engagement of the platform, shouting out its wide array of content types.

One of the creators remarked, “I love using Instagram,” calling it “one of the best social platforms around.”.

The next most-used social media platform is TikTok. Many of the creators we talk to and write about use TikTok as their main platform. Our survey group likes TikTok for its large audience, universal appeal, and fun content.

According to one respondent, it’s the best place to get a start on social media. Once you’ve gotten that start, one creator stated, “It's a good platform for people who want to share their life or creations through short-form videos. Or if they want to post short clips from their longer videos to attract viewers to their YouTube channel.”.

Sources indicate that and that brings us to our creator pool's final favorite social media platform: YouTube. Similar to TikTok, one creator stated, “It's a great place to post your content, whether long or short form, and is used by millions.”.

Others love it for the easy-to-use platform and quality features, calling it “fun and cool” and “better than the other brands.”.

Topics Creators Creators' Choice.

Sources indicate that based in Newly introduced York City, Miller Kern is the Deputy Editor of Shopping and Reviews at Mashable, where she writes and edits reviews, roundups, deals, and news stories about tech products, including headphones, skincare devices, laptops, sex toys, e-readers, robot vacuums, and more. She's been covering all things shopping and tech, including shopping holidays like Prime Day and Black Friday, for Mashable since 2019. Miller can tell you which products are actually worth your money. She also explores trends in the shopping sphere, such as dupes and viral TikTok moments.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Head coach Steven Pressley has admitted that "at times, I've wanted to crawl under a rock and hide" after Dundee's 8-0 "humiliation" by Heart of Midlothian.
  • Two days after the Dens Park debacle, Pressley is still adamant he must shoulder the blame - despite winger Alan Forrest earlier saying the "freak" result was down to the players.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Steven Pressley says there is a "fragility" in the Dundee squad.

Head coach Steven Pressley has admitted that "at times, I've wanted to crawl under a rock and hide" after Dundee's 8-0 "humiliation" by Heart of Midlothian.

Two days after the Dens Park debacle, Pressley is still adamant he must shoulder the blame - despite winger Alan Forrest earlier saying the "freak" result was down to the players.

Pressley said after the game he was concerned a poor result was imminent and admits he had sensed some complacency within the squad.

"Our strength has been built on cohesion, unity and aggressiveness," said the head coach, who said he was embarrassed by the result but that at difficult times he "seems to find strength from somewhere".

"I think Saturday highlighted exactly what I've been saying - if we get lazy on the hard yards, we're a very vulnerable team.

"We have to be, as I've been consistent all along, at our absolute best to get results.

"I've sensed a little bit of subconscious complacency and my job is to ensure that doesn't seep into their performance.".

Pressley on wanting to 'crawl under a rock', complacency & 'direct' culture.

Hearts bounce back from 'rocky patch' with Dens 'demolition'.

Pressley believes "there is a little bit of fragility in the squad - certain players of huge talent but a little bit fragile mentally" and must now lift them to face a Hibernian side on Tuesday who are hurting from a 4-0 home defeat by Dundee United.

"It's been a difficult 24, 48 hours," he admitted. "There's been a lot of hurt, a lot of embarrassment.

"At times, I've wanted to crawl under a rock and hide on the back of such a disappointing result.

According to recent reports, "But I will say this, you know I suffer a lot from vulnerability at times, but for some reason during difficult moments, I seem to find strength from somewhere. I do and I've had to show strength.

"But we had a good meeting on Sunday. We chatted a lot about the various aspects and hopefully we can start responding to the disappointment.".

Pressley noted he knew pre-match "that we're nowhere near as good as people tell us we are" and he had previously tried "various things" to guard against a poor performance.

"I've been trying to introduce a couple of things within their training, within our debriefs on games," he revealed.

"But obviously what I have tried to do hasn't had the right effect and, when you get a performance like Saturday, which lacked that intensity, lacked those hard yards, that's on me because I have to make sure that they're ready for that.".

It was the first time the former Scotland centre-half has suffered such a heavy defeat as a player or manager.

"There's been some really disappointing days, disappointing results, but of course when you're the head coach and it's my responsibility then this ranks as one of the worst," he added.

"I've been in football for nearly 36 years and you think what have I not experienced and then this comes along. It's the great thing about football - it just keeps testing you.

"We have to use days like this as a reminder to ourselves - as a reset moment. I just hope we can bring some pride back to the football club with the right type of performance against Hibs.".

Mabel Willis turned 11 on Sunday, and her proud mom marked the occasion by sharing a montage of family photos and videos taken over the years, set to the song “Pictures Of You” by The Cure.

“Happy 11th Birthday Mabel Ray!” Heming Willis wrote in the caption.

“Your energy is infectious,” she continued, praising her little girl for the way she “can light a whole room with your smile and warmth.”.

Heming Willis and Willis married in 2009. Along with Mabel, the couple also have an 8-year-old daughter, Evelyn. Willis also has daughters Rumer, Scout and Tallulah with his ex-wife, Demi Moore.

It has been revealed that willis is clearly a doting dad. One picture in Heming Willis’ montage indicates the “Die Hard” star holding baby Mabel while planting a kiss on her forehead, while a more recent image shows a beaming Willis hanging out in nature with his preteen.

Bruce Willis sings with his family in birthday tribute video from ex Demi Moore.

Heming Willis penned an equally heartfelt tribute last month when her husband celebrated his 68th birthday. Sharing a video montage on Instagram, she referred to the actor as “pure love.”.

In February, Willis’ family confirmed that his speaking disorder, aphasia, had progressed into a form of dementia called frontotemporal dementia, or FTD.

“Today there are no treatments for the disease, a reality that we hope can change in the years ahead,” they stated in an upgrade shared online. “As Bruce’s condition advances, we hope that any media attention can be focused on shining a light on this disease that needs far more awareness and research.”.

According to the Alzheimer’s Association, FTD refers to “a group of disorders caused by progressive nerve cell loss in the brain’s frontal lobes (the areas behind your forehead) or its temporal lobes.” These areas of the brain are generally associated with personality, behavior and language.

In a recent development, in the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very vital,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. According to recent reports, with that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. Latest Update: Turkey takes control of opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (780 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that another key opposition media outlet in Turkey has been placed under state control.
  • A trustee has also been appointed: The state deposit protection fund, TMSF, which usually administers the assets of insolvent companies, has been put in charge.
  • A large police contingent raided the broadcaster's headquarters in Istanbul, with counterterrorism officers searching the offices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that another key opposition media outlet in Turkey has been placed under state control. On Tuesday morning, authorities raided the offices of the television broadcaster Sozcu TV and the news portal Sozcu.com.tr, and arrested several executives.

A trustee has also been appointed: The state deposit protection fund, TMSF, which usually administers the assets of insolvent companies, has been put in charge. Sozcu was one of the last big media companies in Turkey to regularly report critically on the government of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

A large police contingent raided the broadcaster's headquarters in Istanbul, with counterterrorism officers searching the offices. According to Sozcu, its chairwoman, Funda Tuncer Sidali, and Asim Akgul, the former chief executive of the Sozcu group, were among those arrested.

The broadcaster did not initially announce the appointment of the trustee on its digital channels. It did call on its audience to follow it under a latest account. The leader of the main opposition party, Ozgur Ozel, declared on X: "You will never be able to prevent this nation's voice from rising, its rebellion from being heard, its cry from echoing.".

Recent findings suggest that the Istanbul public prosecutor's office has confirmed the arrangements. It justified the investigation with claims of a suspected connection between the owner of Sozcu, Burak Akhay, and the Gülen movement. The Turkish government blames this movement, which was once allied to Erdogan, for the attempted coup in 2016, and has designated it a terrorist organization.

Recent findings suggest that according to the investigators, Akbay is said to have used foreign bank accounts to finance two companies involved in media activities on behalf of the Gülen movement. They claim there is strong suspicion that he was able, in this way, to hold a leadership position in the organization.

Industry observers note that it is not new for the Turkish state to take over media organizations by appointing trustees. Many media companies accused of being close to the Gülen movement were brought under state control in this way after the attempted coup in 2016. What is new is that for about a year now this is also happening to media seen as pro-opposition.

Recent findings suggest that sozcu is not the first opposition broadcaster to be targeted by the authorities. The TELEI TV channel was searched on October 24, 2025. Its editor-in-chief, Merdan Yanardag, was arrested on charges of espionage and remains in custody. The offices of Halk TV were raided on October 14 this year. There, too, a trustee was put in charge.

Sources indicate that in the space of just over a year, three of the most notable opposition television channels have been brought under state control. Observers see this as another step toward an increasingly authoritarian and politically isolated system.

Berk Esen, a political scientist with Sabanci University in Istanbul, sees these measures as a significant weakening of the opposition in the public domain.

In a recent development, esen told DW that the government may first have acted behind the scenes and tried to bring Sozcu to heel politically. When this didn't succeed, it invoked the judiciary. Esen indicates Turkey is increasingly moving toward an authoritarian system. The attempt to prevent opposition organizations and media from gaining strength and influence is part of this.

Esen describes the opposition's success in local government elections in March 2024 as a political turning point. Since then, he claims, the government has seen its chances of winning political competitions at the ballot box receding. "It's become harder for the AKP to win elections," says Esen. "That's why it's attacking the opposition and the free media both at once.".

Several opposition mayors have also been arrested in recent months and replaced by trustees. They include the mayor of Istanbul and presidential candidate Ekrem Imamoglu, who has been in detention since his arrest in March last year. He is regarded as one of Erdogan's most promising challengers.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The Turkish Journalists' Association (TGC) spoke of a "black winter for press freedom," and announced its solidarity with all those affected. It described the recent developments as a serious attack on press freedom. The fact that a trustee had been appointed, first at Halk TV and now at Sozcu, revealed how the media climate in Turkey has deteriorated, it said.

Industry observers note that "These days, too, shall pass," the TGC declared. "When that day comes, those journalists who seek the truth today will be remembered, as will the decisions that prevent the public from hearing that truth.".

When is the Euro 2028 qualifying draw?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The home nations have been allocated their pots for Euro 2028 qualifying.
  • The Euro 2028 qualifying draw will take place on Sunday, 6 December at 17:00 GMT at the International Convention Centre in Belfast.
  • It will form the twelve groups that make up the qualifying group stage; six containing four teams and six containing five teams.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The home nations have been allocated their pots for Euro 2028 qualifying.

The Euro 2028 qualifying draw will take place on Sunday, 6 December at 17:00 GMT at the International Convention Centre in Belfast.

It will form the twelve groups that make up the qualifying group stage; six containing four teams and six containing five teams.

All 54 Uefa member associations will enter qualifying at the group stage.

Despite hosting the 2028 tournament, the UK home nations and the Republic of Ireland must also participate in qualifying rounds.

England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland will host the Euro 2028 tournament.

The 54 teams have been divided into five pots based on their interim overall ranking in the 2026-27 Nations League following the conclusion of the league phase.

Pots one to four contain 12 teams, and pot five contains six teams.

The teams will then be drawn into the 12 qualifying groups, with the four host teams, as well as Northern Ireland, drawn into different groups.

The four winners of the Nations League quarter-finals must be drawn into a group containing four teams.

According to recent reports, twenty teams, made up of 12 group winners and eight best runners-up, will advance directly to the tournament proper. The eight highest-ranking runners-up will be based on the overall qualifying rankings.

If host nations fail to win or are runners-up in their group, there will be two spaces in the tournament proper reserved for the best-ranked nations at the end of the group stage, regardless of how many other host nation teams have qualified.

As a result, the final number of teams in the tournament proper will be between 20 and 22 nations, depending on the performance of the host nations.

There are also qualifying routes available through the 2026-27 Nations League.

Nations League final rankings will also determine the seeding of nations for Euro 2028 qualification.

You can read more on how the process works here.

Pot One: England, Portugal, France, Germany, Spain, Belgium, Netherlands, Norway, Greece, Italy, Denmark, Croatia.

Pot Two: Wales, Serbia, Turkey, Czech Republic, Switzerland, Sweden, Austria, Northern Ireland, Slovenia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Hungary, Republic of Ireland.

Pot Three: Ukraine, Scotland, Kosovo, Poland, Israel, Romania, Georgia, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Albania, Iceland, Slovakia.

Pot Four: Estonia, Belarus, Faroe Islands, Cyprus, Finland, Moldova, Armenia, Bulgaria, Kazakhstan, Luxembourg, Latvia, San Marino.

Pot Five: Malta, Azerbaijan, Lithuania, Andorra, Gibraltar, Liechtenstein.

Matchday three: 11-12 June 2027.

Matchday five: 23-25 September 2027.

Matchday six: 26-28 September 2027.

Matchday seven: 30 September-2 October 2027.

Matchday eight: 3-5 October 2027.

Matchday nine: 11-13 November 2027.

Matchday 10: 14-16 November 2027.

Wembley Stadium will host two of England's group-stage matches should they qualify for the final tournament.

If the host nations and/or Northern Ireland qualify for the tournament proper, they will have dedicated slots at stadiums:.

England (Group B): Etihad Stadium (one match), Wembley Stadium (two matches).

Northern Ireland (Group D): Tottenham Hotspur Stadium (one match), Villa Park (one match), Wembley Stadium (one match).

Republic of Ireland (Group E): Dublin Arena (three matches).

Scotland (Group F): Hampden Park (three matches).

Wales (Group A): National Stadium of Wales (three matches).

If the hosts and/or Northern Ireland qualify via the play-offs, they will still be assigned to their designated group, but will not play all their group matches in the locations mentioned above.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Space ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Voyager 1 team, unbowed by communications glitch, celebrates epic 1-light-day distance milestone

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1694 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • – NASA's Voyager mission team cheered and wiped away tears here on Thursday (Nov.
  • Sources indicate that voyager team members gathered for a press conference about the mission at the Von Karman auditorium here at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) — the first such Voyager event since 1989, when Voyager 1's twin, Voyager 2, flew past Neptune.
  • "I remember in 1977 I was standing at the Cape watching Voyager launch, and I never thought I would be here today, 49 years later, to celebrate Voyager's one light-day.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

PASADENA, Calif. – NASA's Voyager mission team cheered and wiped away tears here on Thursday (Nov. 19), celebrating a big milestone — Voyager 1 just reached one light-day from Earth, something no other spacecraft has ever done. The excitement persisted despite a communication anomaly that cropped up on the probe, which the team remains confident is temporary.

Sources indicate that voyager team members gathered for a press conference about the mission at the Von Karman auditorium here at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) — the first such Voyager event since 1989, when Voyager 1's twin, Voyager 2, flew past Neptune. The gathering served to celebrate Voyager 1's distance milestone: At 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT) on Wednesday (Nov. 18), the probe reached one light-day from Earth — the distance a photon travels in one day, which is about 16 billion miles (26 billion kilometers). That means it now takes a full day for a signal to travel from Earth to Voyager 1, the farthest human-made object out in space.

"I remember in 1977 I was standing at the Cape watching Voyager launch, and I never thought I would be here today, 49 years later, to celebrate Voyager's one light-day. What an incredible milestone," Voyager project scientist Linda Spilker said during Thursday's event.

While this day and this week have been chock-full of excitement over the distance milestone, the Voyager mission team has been hard at work, as usual, keeping the two nearly 50-year-old spacecraft alive and functioning.

Industry observers note that unfortunately, as JPL spokesperson Raquel Villanueva shared at this celebration, on Saturday (Nov. 14), Voyager 1 stopped transmitting science and engineering data. The team has remained in contact with Voyager 1 while investigating the issue, and they are confident that they'll be able to solve it soon.

"We listen to each spacecraft every day," Voyager project manager Suzanne Dodd told Space.com at the event. Regarding Voyager 1, "we have an anomaly that is not something unseen before," Dodd stated. "We do have a very strong carrier signal. We currently don't have a frame sync, so we're not getting the science or engineering data currently.".

According to recent reports, "But if you recall," Dodd added, "one light-day is very far from us. [It takes] 24 hours to get the signal to the spacecraft, 24 hours for the signal to come down, so it takes two days to diagnose anything on the spacecraft … So we can't do anything fast, and the data rates are very low.".

Industry observers note that according to Dodd, this anomaly isn't a major cause for long-term concern. Rather, it's likely just part of the natural aging process for spacecraft.

It has been revealed that "These spacecraft are old," she mentioned. "All of us old people have our aches and pains, and you know, sometimes it takes longer to stretch out your muscles and remember things, and so we are in a realm where we're going to see more anomalies with Voyager just due to the distance and the age.".

In a recent development, "But we feel Voyager 1, although it's not sending us the telemetry data, it's pointed at the Earth. It's sending us a strong carrier signal, and I'm confident that it won't be too long, and it will send us data back.".

And, for anyone curious how Voyager 1's slower twin Voyager 2 is faring, Dodd shared that it is doing very well on its own journey through interstellar space. "Voyager 2 is very healthy. It's continuing its mission. It has three scientific instruments on it," she told Space.com.

"Each spacecraft is basically setting a record every day for longevity or distance," Dodd added about the twin probes.

Despite the communications anomaly — and even though most of the team had been up all night to confirm the one-light-day signal from Voyager 1 — the room was alive with excitement. The Voyagers have been flying for nearly 50 years on a mission expected to last just five years, so the team was beyond ready to celebrate.

It has been revealed that amidst the more technical updates about the mission and its current status out in interstellar space, the event included footage of Voyager light-day celebrations from around the world. From children cheering on Voyager to iconic landmarks lighting up gold in honor of the mission's Golden Record, the Voyager love echoed around the world in photos and videos. The footage of this international celebration was enough to move Nicky Fox, NASA's associate administrator for the Science Mission Directorate, nearly to tears.

It has been revealed that "I actually thought I was going to start sobbing," Fox joked to Space.com after the media briefing. "I think just hearing children's voices and people saying 'We love you, Voyager,' 'Go Voyager' — it just was amazing.".

Industry observers note that and Fox and the mission team members weren't the only ones sharing their love for Voyager. NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins beamed down her own video message to the Voyager 1 spacecraft from the International Space Station, sharing in the celebration.

Recent findings suggest that "Dear Voyager 1," Watkins stated. "As an orbiting outpost just 250 miles [400 kilometers] above Earth, we often feel distant yet deeply connected to our home planet. The International Space Station has had crew continuously living off of the Earth for 26 years, seen hundreds of visitors from around the world, and enabled thousands of experiments to advance space exploration.

In a recent development, "While you have been traveling into the unknown for nearly half a century, helping pave our path, together, our two journeys tell a single story of exploration," she continued. "One remains close to home, and the other reaches ever outward. Voyager 1, you have been a beacon of light, a symbol of exploration, a seeker of truth, a carrier of hope, a brave explorer, traveling further than any human hand has ever reached. You represent the very best of what humanity has to offer.

"As you reach a distance of one light-day from Earth, the entire crew of Expedition 75 and people across the planet send you our admiration and our wishes for a safe and continued journey as you begin your post-one-light-day era. There are so many amazing milestones and discoveries to come. You have a universe ahead of you, and you carry with you our collective hopes and dreams. When we look up from Earth, we will always think of you as you continue forward into the great unknown. May you continue shining bright for all of us. Go Voyager 1!" Watkins mentioned, ending her message with a weightless backflip from aboard the station.

In concluding the media briefing, the mission team invited those in the room who, over the past 50 years (or more, with one person sharing their excitement having worked on Voyager before it was even called Voyager) have worked on the mission in one way or another, to stand up to a round of applause. With mission team members today ranging from those in their 20s to their 90s, the people behind this enduring mission span many generations.

Interestingly, Fox actually began her light-day celebrations earlier in the week. She, alongside writer/producer Ann Druyan — who was the wife of the late astronomer Carl Sagan, whose work helped create the mission's Golden Record and who took the now-famous "pale blue dot" Voyager image of Earth to the public — together lit up the Empire State Building gold.

According to recent reports, "I was actually very privileged to flick the switch and turn on the Empire State Building lights on Tuesday evening [Nov. 17]," Fox, wearing golden Voyager-inspired nail polish crafted by her daughter, told Space.com. "That was just spectacular … I was there with Ann … we were both so giddy with the excitement of doing it … It was amazing. And then going up and standing underneath and seeing the tower was just really, really special.".

While the room lit up with excitement for Voyager's light-day milestone on Thursday, the team was also brimming with anticipation for what lies ahead. As Voyager hurtles toward another major milestone, turning 50 in 2027, it remains an active science mission, and the team remains hard at work to push the boundaries of exploration with these aging probes.

Industry observers note that "Voyager right now — the two Voyagers — they're in an area of space that we've never been into. So every single bit of data that comes back is precious because it's unique," Fox said.

Recent findings suggest that "Now we're in a region where the sun's influence is a lot different, and we're in this region where we can start to understand: What is it like out past our sun? What is it like in the space between the stars?" Voyager deputy project scientist Jamie Rankin told Space.com. "We're at a very exciting time of starting to connect what we know and what we've seen, living with this star [our sun] to what is out there.".

Sources indicate that "What's next? Voyager is just going to keep on going. You know, people sometimes think, 'When's the mission going to end?' It's never going to end," Fox added to Space.com. "Even when we can no longer talk to Voyager, they're both going to keep going … So there's no end for the Voyager mission.".

With a M.S. in Biology, Chelsea has written and worked for institutions including NASA JPL, the American Museum of Natural History, Scientific American, Discover Magazine Blog, Astronomy Magazine, and Live Science. When not writing, editing or filming something space-y, Gohd is writing music and performing as Foxanne, even launching a song to space in 2021 with Inspiration4. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • European Union top officials and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham confirmed deals on trade and youth mobility at Friday's Brussels summit.
  • This might be the first step to rebuild ties, a decade after Britain voted to leave the EU.
  • During the delegations' meeting, Burnham said the deal was a "landmark agreement," while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called it a "turning point" in relations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

European Union top officials and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham confirmed deals on trade and youth mobility at Friday's Brussels summit.

This might be the first step to rebuild ties, a decade after Britain voted to leave the EU.

During the delegations' meeting, Burnham said the deal was a "landmark agreement," while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called it a "turning point" in relations.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"This is a good day for Britain. This is a good day for Europe," Burnham said.

Speaking at the joint press conference, European Council President Antonio Costa said the bloc respected the British decision to leave the EU and would respect its choice to strengthen ties in the post-Brexit era.

He stated jokingly that the EU and UK "may drive on the opposite sides of the road, but what matters is they are heading for the same direction.".

Burnham stated that the deals were made with young people in mind, adding: "This deal is for you. This deal really is about lifting your life chances.".

He went further and noted "Brexit took opportunities from young people," and that they have to "open up new opportunities" for young people.

Von der Leyen stated the youth experience project would "open horizons and create friendships that will last a lifetime.".

She mentioned the trade agreement is a "two way street" and it means "more choice for the customers.".

Von der Leyen also mentioned the agreement on the carbon market, saying that it would cut emissions and generate investments in cleaner industries.

She also noted Britain will rejoin the Erasmus+ program, adding, "We miss them so much.".

Burnham said the agreements reached Friday, however, represent the most the UK could achieve at the moment, "What we are announcing today is probably ‌the limit of what we can achieve in this ‌Parliament, given what needs ‌to be done to implement it.".

In September, Burnham remarked he would seek a political consensus on the country's future relationship with the EU, even suggesting he could campaign to take Britain back into the bloc at the next election.

Industry observers note that "Britain and Europe share values, interests and a global neighborhood. In a more dangerous world, we are stronger together. A closer partnership with Europe is good for working people, good for Britain and good for Europe," Burnham said as he arrived in Brussels.

The three key agreements establish ways to:.

The "youth experience scheme" would allow 100,000 people under 30 from each side to reside for up to three years in each other's territory for work, study or travel without being subject to existing visa requirements.

No deal was reached on tuition fees for EU students studying in Britain, a deal-breaker for the bloc. The EU has pressed for the UK to reduce university tuition fees for EU students to the same level paid by British students.

"There will be further discussions coming out of it on issues including on tuition fees," Burnham noted.

Von der Leyen ‌said ⁠she was confident negotiators would reach a ​solution ​on ‌tuition fees, "We will be working ‌on that in ‌the ​next month and as we have a ​track record of finding ⁠solutions,.".

Sources indicate that on the food deal, the EU and UK have agreed to scrap certificates and border checks on food and animal products to ease post-Brexit trade. In return, Britain will align more closely with EU food safety and animal health rules.

They also agreed to link their emissions-trading systems, allowing them to recognize each other's carbon allowances and exempt traded goods from carbon border taxes.

According to the AFP news agency, London estimates the deal could boost the British economy by 3.8 billion pounds annually, and spare 6.5 billion pounds worth of steel, aluminum and other industrial exports from additional taxation.

Leaders mentioned they will establish a "structured dialogue on migration." Their joint summit statement said this would include "engagement with third countries" and "returns to third countries," among other issues.

The two sides agreed to launch formal talks on economic security and strengthen cooperation on export controls and supply chains, among other areas.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

On Monday, Burnham stated it ​was the "obvious truth" that ‌Britain had lost more than it had gained from Brexit.

Polling firm YouGov runs a regular tracker on whether the UK was right or wrong to vote to quit.

Since mid-2022, a majority of people surveyed said Britain was wrong to leave.In September, the "Bregret" camp rose to 60% — the highest ever.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rio Ngumoha is going to be a 'wow' player for Liverpool - and he highlighted everyone exactly what he is already capable of in Sunday's 4-0 win over Manchester United.

He made an outstanding assist then added a fine finish, and there is much more to come. He plays without fear so he is going to score and make many more goals the same way.

Ngumoha has only just turned 18 but he is already a game-changer, someone who gets people excited because he is so hard to stop when he is one-on-one.

Of course he can frustrate you at times too, but that's what creative and explosive wingers like him do - and it's because he is so talented that everyone wants to see an end product from him every time he gets on the ball.

There were times against United when Ngumoha did not quite deliver, but he is still so young and I would much rather see players like him take too many touches - or try too many things and fail - than be afraid to try them in the first place.

So, if he runs out of play or runs into too many players at times, because teams are doubling up on him like United were, that just shows how scared they are of him.

His ability means he occupies opposition players - Youri Tielemans was always backing up Diogo Dalot on his wing to try to help him out, but that just meant United were leaving someone else free.

Ngumoha stars as Liverpool thrash 10-man Man Utd.

Sometimes it is actually harder when you are playing out wide against 10 men because you don't get the same amount of space - United were not attacking the same way they would have done with 11, and they were sitting in more.

Industry observers note that yes, Ngumoha ran up the odd blind alley or got outnumbered but that is always going to happen. As he learns, and gets even better, his decision-making will improve too. He will know when to try to go past people or when to find that free man instead.

But he still showed all the bravery you want from a winger against United and, when you keep trying things the way he did, something is going to come off for you.

I look at Bradley Barcola in a similar way to Ngumoha - he can be frustrating but he tries things, and can be brilliant.

For Liverpool right now, one of the biggest positives is the competition they have in wide areas, with those two plus Victor Munoz and Cody Gakpo.

There are other areas of their squad, like left-back or central midfield, where that competition needs to improve, but I don't really worry about the wide attacking areas in the same way.

Sunday was only Ngumoha's second Premier League start of the season, and his first since the opening day.

He maybe only got his chance because Gakpo has a calf problem but, when everyone is fit, it is really exciting that they will all be thinking they have to play their best to push the manager and get in the team.

Andoni Iraola post-match interview - Liverpool v Man Utd.

It has been revealed that there were plenty of other positives for Liverpool, too. All in all, Sunday could not have gone much better for them.

United made a woeful start with poor concentration and mistakes which cost them but, from there, Liverpool saw the game out well.

Just because the opposition has a man sent off early on does not mean any kind of victory is a given, let alone a 4-0 win.

Look at how United's 11 men lost to City's 10 in the Manchester derby earlier this season - we've seen many times how good teams can frustrate a side with an extra player like that.

It definitely does not mean you are going to steamroller them, but Liverpool did that and made an abundance of chances to get even more goals.

Days like this are so crucial for building belief in all their attacking players, especially because they were playing at home, and against their massive rivals.

Up until now, it had felt like Liverpool's better days this season had come on the road, but now the pressure and expectation is off them a bit - particularly if, like Ngumoha or Florian Wirtz, you have scored and played well.

I know from experience that, the next time they go back to Anfield, they will be buzzing. You know that the fans are already with you after you've scored against United, and you feel the love a little bit more.

This is the start of a substantial week for Liverpool and Iraola will probably make changes against Club Brugge in Belgium on Wednesday, knowing how difficult Sunday's Merseyside derby will be.

Everton is always a tough game but I think Liverpool will enjoy their trip to Hill Dickinson Stadium, and the confidence they will have after beating United will mean they can go there with a really positive mindset.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jamie Lee Curtis was honest about her birthday blues.
  • According to recent reports, as the Freaky Friday actress celebrated her 68th birthday Nov.
  • “The long and winding road,” Curtis wrote in a post on Instagram.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jamie Lee Curtis was honest about her birthday blues.

According to recent reports, as the Freaky Friday actress celebrated her 68th birthday Nov. 22, she reflected on the death of her sister Kelly Lee Curtis earlier this year, which made her the only living member of her nuclear family.

“The long and winding road,” Curtis wrote in a post on Instagram. “Another circle around the sun! Today will be the first year, that I am the only surviving family member of my immediate family and my immediate second family. The last in the line. The loss of my sister Kelly in June was a real blow and I feel sad today.”.

Still, Curtis—whose mom Janet Leigh died in 2004, while her father Tony Curtis died in 2010—emphasized the gratitude she has for her life.

“I look back at photographs of me as a child, and I look so stunned to be here at birth, and it carried on through much of my young life, always seemingly startled and slightly concerned,” she continued. “I've worked through a lot of that discomfort, and I'm so happy to be here and have the life I have. Both personal and creative.”.

Meanwhile, Curtis—mom to Annie, 39, and Ruby, 30, with husband Christopher Guest—expressed desire to pass down what she learned from her late loved ones on to her living family members. “What remains for me is the legacy of other humans who forged a path for me to be here through their actions and examples as I hope I am for my own family and of course friends,” the Halloween star continued, “and, as a public person, the millions of people I've involved in my life.”.

And, of course, Curtis knows she is surrounded by love.

“My husband and my daughters and their families and my young grandson, all of whom I get to see today for this life that I love so very much,” the Oscar winner continued. “I wish you all a happy and healthy Thanksgiving and holiday season.”.

For a deeper look into Curtis’ candidness, keep reading….

Amid the chatter surrounding Pamela Anderson and Liam Neeson’s rumored romance, Jamie Lee Curtis swiftly shut down any of the Naked Gun stars’ possible detractors.

According to recent reports, “With all due respect to pop culture, if love has found [its] way into that relationship—God bless them both—leave them the f--k alone,” the Everything Everywhere All At Once actress told VT in August 2025. “Let them like each other. Both of them have had hardship, and they’re both beautiful human beings.”.

And she further took a moment to heap praise on her Last Showgirl costar Anderson.

“She’s a beautiful person,” Curtis added, “She was fantastic [in the movie], but she’s a beautiful human being.”.

The actress—daughter to the late Tony Curtis and Janet Leigh—hasn’t held back when it comes to sharing how seeing her parents’ later careers has shaped how she views longevity in Hollywood, and why it makes her more intentional about what she takes on.

“I have been prepping to get out, so that I don’t have to suffer the same was as my family did,” Curtis opened up to The Guardian in a July 2025 interview. “I want to leave the party before I’m no longer invited. I witnessed my parents lose the very thing that gave them their fame and their life and their livelihood, when the industry rejected them at a certain age.”.

And she doesn’t want to be hurt in the same way. “I watched them reach incredible success and then have it slowly erode to where it was gone,” she continued. “And that’s very painful.”.

As for her decades long career, Curtis considers herself an “old lady” jokingly adding, “I’m going to die soon.”.

She takes bedtime seriously—and that’s why she doesn’t want to go to a concert in the evening. In fact, she has a proposition for singers.

“I’m challenging musicians to do concerts during the day,” Curtis posited on Today in March. “Why are there no matinees? For instance, I love Coldplay, I would love to go see Coldplay. I would love it, but the problem is I am not going to see Coldplay if they start their show at nine and there is an opening act. I want to hear Coldplay at 1 p.m.”.

As for how the Academy Award winner wants to turn this dream into a reality?

“I think if we filled a stadium of people who want to see a matinee of Coldplay,” she continued, “I think we’re going to start a trend.”.

The Freaky Friday star proved she was a true Californian by leaving film’s biggest night early to satiate her fast-food craving at the beloved West Coast joint.

“FLY IN [check emoji],” Curtis posted on Instagram March 2024 with a photo featuring her getting a meal at In-and-Out, “GET FLUFFED AND FOLDED [check emoji] PRESENT AT OSCARS [check emoji] GO TO @inandout_burger [check emoji] FLY AWAY.”.

Walking Back Her Not-So Marvelous Take on Superhero Movies.

After not holding back by saying a more recent phase of Marvel Cinematic Universe was “bad,” the Knives Out actress subsequently admitted she regretted her comments on the superhero movie franchise.

“My comments about Marvel were stupid and I will do better,” Curtis, who had previously shaded the Doctor Strange movies while promoting her own multiverse movie Everything Everywhere All at Once, wrote on X in August 2024.“I’ve reached out to Kevin Feige and will no longer play in that mud slinging sandbox of competition we call the internet nor will I engage in the toilet paper promotion or game play that is designed for clicks not content or conversation.”.

For Curtis, a negative comment from a cinematographer while filming the 1985 movie Perfect alongside John Travolta resulted in an eye-opening experience with cosmetic procedures.

Sources indicate that “He was like, ‘Yeah I’m not shooting her today. Her eyes are baggy,” she remarked on 60 minutes in May. “I was 25. For him to say that was very embarrassing. So as soon as the movie finished, I ended up having some plastic surgery.”.

“That’s just not what you want to do when you’re 25 or 26,” she continued, “I regretted it immediately and have sort of regretted it since.”.

And it influenced the way she views cosmetic enhancements.

“I’ve become a really public advocate,” Curtis explained, “to say to women, ‘You’re gorgeous and you’re perfect the way you are,’ so,…oh yeah. It was not a good thing for me to do.”.

If your current morning ritual involves violently hitting refresh on a dozen retail tabs, you already know the vibe: finding the Nintendo Switch 2: The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition is turning into an Olympic sport.

Industry observers note that we're closely monitoring inventory at all the major retailers and are cautiously optimistic it will be restocked for the holiday shopping season. Before getting into the restock details, bookmark these retailer pages to check for surprise drops:.

Nintendo Store — Out of stock right now, but you can add it to your wishlist to get pinged the second a restock hits.

Amazon — Dropping tiny batches of consoles randomly throughout the day.

The feeding frenzy is being supercharged by Nintendo’s staggered release calendar. While the custom Zelda 40th Anniversary hardware dropped first on Oct. 29, the flagship game driving demand — The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Nintendo Switch 2 — arrived on Thursday, Nov. 5.

The remake rebuilds the 1998 classic from the ground up with modernized controls, a fully orchestrated soundtrack, reworked dungeon puzzles, and expanded Hyrule environments. Since the $520 console doesn’t include the game, everyone is rushing to lock down a system before launch day.

It retains the platform's signature flexibility, letting you switch between TV, Tabletop, and Handheld modes whenever you want. Landing limited-edition Nintendo hardware takes a little prep work, but these battle-tested habits will give you a real edge over the bots:.

Hands off the refresh button in Best Buy's queue — When an online drop goes live, Best Buy puts shoppers into a randomized waiting line to filter out scrapers. Touching the reload button resets your spot and boots you straight to the back.

Industry observers note that watch for Walmart+ early-access paywalls — Walmart frequently locks headline console drops behind paid Walmart+ subscriptions for the first 30 to 60 minutes. If you have a membership, keep that tab signed in; if not, wait for the general public window to unlock.

Recent findings suggest that dodge third-party sellers — Double-check the seller before buying. Marketplace scalpers frequently list units for jacked-up prices; make sure it states "Sold and shipped by [Retailer]" at the standard price.

It has been revealed that skip the web wars and head to physical stores — Online checkout bots grab website stock in under 15 seconds. Showing up in person is easily your most reliable path to securing one without paying scalper markups.

If you can grab a console whenever stock appears, take it. Think of Black Friday as a backup strategy, not your main bet.

#94111. SpaceX Dragon cargo capsule returns to Earth from the ISS
